exercises.question: I have a _____.
exercises.explanation: El adjetivo va ANTES del sustantivo: new car.

exercises.question: The house _____ big.
exercises.explanation: Después de un sujeto singular usamos 'is' + adjetivo.

exercises.question: She has _____ phone.
exercises.explanation: Antes de adjetivos que empiezan con vocal usamos 'an'.

exercises.question: The students _____ happy.
exercises.explanation: Plural (students) usa 'are'.

exercises.question: My city is _____. (beautiful)
exercises.explanation: Después de 'is' va el adjetivo solo, no se repite el sustantivo.

exercises.question: I have an _____ car. (old)
exercises.explanation: El adjetivo va entre el artículo y el sustantivo.

exercises.question: These are _____ children. (happy)
exercises.explanation: Los adjetivos en inglés NO cambian con el plural.

exercises.question: The house is big house.
exercises.explanation: Después del verbo 'to be' NO se repite el sustantivo, solo va el adjetivo.

exercises.question: I have a car new.
exercises.explanation: El adjetivo va ANTES del sustantivo, no después.

exercises.question: The students is happy.
exercises.explanation: Plural 'students' requiere 'are', no 'is'.

exercises.question: She _____ a new bike.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona (she/he/it) usa 'has got'.

exercises.question: We _____ a big house.
exercises.explanation: I/you/we/they usan 'have got'.

exercises.question: _____ you got a car?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'have got': se mueve 'have' al inicio. NO se usa 'do'.

exercises.question: _____ she have a dog?
exercises.explanation: Versión americana sin 'got': pregunta con 'Does + sujeto + have'.

exercises.question: He _____ a brother.
exercises.explanation: Sin 'got', el negativo de tercera persona es 'doesn't have'.

exercises.question: She _____ got two brothers. (verbo correcto)
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: 'has got'.

exercises.question: I _____ got a dog. (negativo, sin contracción)
exercises.explanation: El negativo de 'have got' es 'haven't got'.

exercises.question: I don't have got a car.
exercises.explanation: No se mezclan las dos formas. O 'I haven't got' o 'I don't have'.

exercises.question: Do you have got a car?
exercises.explanation: Si usás 'do', es la versión sin 'got'.

exercises.question: She have a dog.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular usa 'has', no 'have'.

exercises.question: She _____ play the piano.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' nunca cambia con la persona ni se le agrega -s.

exercises.question: He _____ swim.
exercises.explanation: El negativo de 'can' es 'can't' (cannot). NO se usa 'don't/doesn't'.

exercises.question: _____ you drive?
exercises.explanation: Para preguntar con 'can', se mueve 'can' al inicio.

exercises.question: Can your father cook? — No, _____.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta a 'Can...?' es 'Yes, ... can / No, ... can't'.

exercises.question: We _____ cook pasta. (afirmativo)
exercises.explanation: 'Can' + verbo en infinitivo sin 'to'.

exercises.question: I _____ swim. (negativo, contraído)
exercises.explanation: Negativo: can't (cannot).

exercises.question: He cans speak English.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' NUNCA lleva -s, ni siquiera en tercera persona.

exercises.question: I can to swim.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'can' NO va 'to'.

exercises.question: Do you can drive?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'can': se mueve 'can' al inicio, sin usar 'do'.

exercises.question: She can plays the guitar.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'can' el verbo va en infinitivo sin -s.

exercises.question: He _____ pizza.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona (he/she/it) en presente simple lleva -s.

exercises.question: _____ she like coffee?
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona en pregunta usa 'Does'.

exercises.question: They _____ vegetables.
exercises.explanation: I/you/we/they: 'don't + like' (sin -s).

exercises.question: Does he like football? — Yes, _____.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta: se repite el auxiliar (does), no el verbo.

exercises.question: She _____ tennis. (afirmativo)
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona lleva -s: likes.

exercises.question: We _____ Mondays. (negativo, contraído)
exercises.explanation: Plural: 'don't like' (sin -s en el verbo).

exercises.question: He don't like pizza.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona usa 'doesn't', no 'don't'.

exercises.question: Does she likes chocolate?
exercises.explanation: Si ya usaste 'does', el verbo va sin -s.

exercises.question: He doesn't likes vegetables.
exercises.explanation: La -s aparece UNA vez: o en 'does' o en el verbo, nunca en ambos.

exercises.question: The book is _____ the table.
exercises.explanation: 'On' = encima en contacto con la superficie.

exercises.question: The bakery is _____ the bank and the hospital.
exercises.explanation: 'Between' = entre dos cosas específicas.

exercises.question: My house is _____ the school. (al lado)
exercises.explanation: 'Next to' = al lado de, justo al costado.

exercises.question: The car is _____ the garage.
exercises.explanation: 'In' = dentro de un espacio cerrado.

exercises.question: The market is _____ the cinema. (cruzando la calle)
exercises.explanation: 'Opposite' = enfrente, cruzando la calle.

exercises.question: The cat is _____ the chair. (debajo)
exercises.explanation: 'Under' = debajo de algo.

exercises.question: The airport is _____ from my house. (lejos)
exercises.explanation: 'Far from' = lejos de.

exercises.question: The bus stop is _____ the supermarket. (cerca)
exercises.explanation: 'Near' = cerca de (sin necesidad de 'to').

exercises.question: _____ is my book. (acá, cerca)
exercises.explanation: 'This' = singular, cerca.

exercises.question: _____ are my photos. (cerca, varias)
exercises.explanation: 'These' = plural, cerca.

exercises.question: _____ is a beautiful park over there.
exercises.explanation: 'That' = singular, lejos.

exercises.question: _____ are bus timetables, next to the door.
exercises.explanation: 'Those' = plural, lejos.

exercises.question: Is _____ the bus to Oxford?
exercises.explanation: Singular + cerca = 'this'.

exercises.question: _____ apples are delicious. (cerca, plural)
exercises.explanation: Plural + cerca = 'These'.

exercises.question: _____ is a train timetable. (cerca, singular)
exercises.explanation: Singular + cerca = 'This'.

exercises.question: Is she a teacher? — Yes, _____.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta afirmativa con 'to be': NO se contrae.

exercises.question: Are you tired? — No, _____.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta negativa: 'I'm not' (es la única contracción aceptada con 'I').

exercises.question: Do they speak English? — Yes, _____.
exercises.explanation: Si la pregunta usa 'do', se responde con 'do'.

exercises.question: Can your brother drive? — Yes, _____.
exercises.explanation: Si la pregunta usa 'can', se responde con 'can'.

exercises.question: Have you got a pet? — No, _____.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta a 'have got': 'haven't / hasn't'.

exercises.question: Does she like coffee? — No, _____.
exercises.explanation: Si la pregunta usa 'does', se responde con 'doesn't'.

exercises.question: Are your parents at home? (sí) — Yes, they _____.
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'are' → respuesta con 'are'.

exercises.question: Can you cook? (no) — No, I _____.
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'can' → respuesta negativa con 'can't'.

exercises.question: Yes, I'm.
exercises.explanation: Las respuestas afirmativas cortas con 'to be' NO se contraen.

exercises.question: You meet your teacher in the morning. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 'Good morning' se usa para saludar durante la mañana. 'Good night' es para despedirse de noche.

exercises.question: Your friend asks: 'How are you?' You feel great. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 'I'm fine, thanks' es la respuesta estándar a '¿cómo estás?'.

exercises.question: You meet someone for the first time. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 'Nice to meet you' se dice al conocer a alguien por primera vez.

exercises.question: Someone says 'Thank you'. What do you reply?
exercises.explanation: 'You're welcome' es la respuesta a 'Thank you'. Significa 'de nada'.

exercises.question: You want to pass someone in the street. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 'Excuse me' se usa para pedir permiso de paso o para interrumpir a alguien.

exercises.question: Which greeting is FORMAL?
exercises.explanation: 'Hello' es formal. 'Hi' y 'Hey' son informales.

exercises.question: It is 8 pm. You greet your neighbor. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 'Good evening' es el saludo de la tarde-noche (al llegar). 'Good night' es para despedirse antes de dormir.

exercises.question: Complete the introduction: '___ name is Maria.'
exercises.explanation: 'My name is...' = Mi nombre es... 'My' es el adjetivo posesivo de primera persona.

exercises.question: Your friend is leaving. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 'See you later' es una forma informal de despedirse. También se dice 'Bye' o 'Take care'.

exercises.question: Someone bumps into you. They say ___.
exercises.explanation: 'Sorry' se usa para disculparse. 'Excuse me' es para pedir permiso; 'sorry' es para pedir disculpas.

exercises.question: How do you write the number 15 in English?
exercises.explanation: 15 = fifteen. Atención: no es 'fiveteen'.

exercises.question: How do you write 21 in English?
exercises.explanation: Los números compuestos del 21 al 99 se escriben con guion: twenty-one, thirty-two, etc.

exercises.question: What is the ordinal of 1?
exercises.explanation: Los tres primeros ordinales son irregulares: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd).

exercises.question: How do you say 5th in words?
exercises.explanation: 5th = fifth. Es irregular: no es 'fiveth'.

exercises.question: Today is May ___. (el 3 de mayo)
exercises.explanation: Las fechas usan ordinales: 'May third' o 'the third of May'.

exercises.question: How do you say 100 in English?
exercises.explanation: 100 = a hundred (o one hundred). No se agrega -s al final.

exercises.question: What is 2nd in words?
exercises.explanation: 2nd = second. Es el segundo ordinal irregular.

exercises.question: How do you say the number 0?
exercises.explanation: 0 se puede decir 'zero' (formal) u 'oh' (números de teléfono, código postal). 'Nil' se usa en fútbol.

exercises.question: How do you say 40 in English?
exercises.explanation: 40 = forty. Cuidado: no se escribe 'fourty'.

exercises.question: Which is the correct way to write 33?
exercises.explanation: Los números compuestos del 21 al 99 llevan guion: thirty-three.

exercises.question: How do you spell 'cat'?
exercises.explanation: Cat se escribe C-A-T. La 'c' suena /k/ en esta palabra.

exercises.question: Which letters are vowels?
options: a, e, i, o, u, y
exercises.explanation: Las vocales básicas del inglés son: a, e, i, o, u. La 'y' puede actuar como vocal pero no es una vocal básica.

exercises.question: Someone asks: 'How do you spell your name?' Your name is Ann. You say:
exercises.explanation: Para deletrear se dice 'It's' + las letras. O también: 'A-N-N'.

exercises.question: How do you spell 'book'?
exercises.explanation: Book: B-O-O-K. Tiene dos O juntas.

exercises.question: Which word has a SILENT letter?
exercises.explanation: En 'knife', la K no se pronuncia. Es una letra silenciosa.

exercises.question: How do you spell 'happy'?
exercises.explanation: Happy tiene doble P: H-A-P-P-Y.

exercises.question: The English alphabet has ___ letters.
exercises.explanation: El alfabeto inglés tiene 26 letras, de la A a la Z.

exercises.question: Which of these is a CAPITAL letter?
exercises.explanation: T es mayúscula (capital letter). a, m, s son minúsculas (lowercase letters).

exercises.question: How do you spell 'school'?
exercises.explanation: School: S-C-H-O-O-L. Tiene 'ch' y doble O.

exercises.question: Your teacher says: 'Write your name in ___.' (letras grandes para título)
exercises.explanation: 'Capital letters' = mayúsculas. 'Lowercase' = minúsculas.

exercises.question: Which day comes after Monday?
exercises.explanation: El orden de los días: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

exercises.question: What is the third month of the year?
exercises.explanation: Los meses en orden: January, February, March, April... March es el tercero.

exercises.question: Today is ___. (lunes)
exercises.explanation: Los días de la semana siempre se escriben con mayúscula en inglés: Monday, Tuesday...

exercises.question: Which month is in summer (in the northern hemisphere)?
exercises.explanation: En el hemisferio norte, el verano (summer) es en junio, julio y agosto. July = julio.

exercises.question: What season is December in Argentina?
exercises.explanation: En Argentina (hemisferio sur), diciembre es verano (summer). Las estaciones son opuestas al hemisferio norte.

exercises.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
exercises.explanation: Los días van con mayúscula (Tuesday), y la oración empieza con mayúscula (Today). Solo la primera letra de la oración y el día llevan mayúscula.

exercises.question: What month comes before December?
exercises.explanation: El orden: ...October, November, December. November es el mes 11.

exercises.question: The last day of the school week is ___.
exercises.explanation: La semana laboral/escolar va de Monday a Friday. Friday es el último día.

exercises.question: Autumn is also called ___.
exercises.explanation: Autumn y fall son sinónimos. 'Fall' es más común en inglés americano, 'autumn' en inglés británico.

exercises.question: What month is it? ___ March.
exercises.explanation: Para decir el mes se usa 'It's + mes': It's March. 'It' es impersonal aquí.

exercises.question: Carlos ___ a student.
exercises.explanation: Carlos = tercera persona singular → 'is'.

exercises.question: I ___ from Argentina.
exercises.explanation: Con 'I' siempre se usa 'am'.

exercises.question: We ___ happy today.
exercises.explanation: 'We' es plural → 'are'.

exercises.question: The short form of 'she is' is ___.
exercises.explanation: La contracción de 'she is' es 'she's'. El apóstrofe reemplaza la 'i' de 'is'.

exercises.question: They ___ teachers.
exercises.explanation: 'They' es plural → 'are'.

exercises.question: The dog ___ small.
exercises.explanation: 'The dog' = tercera persona singular → 'is'.

exercises.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
exercises.explanation: 'I' siempre va con 'am', nunca con 'is' o 'are'.

exercises.question: The short form of 'they are' is ___.
exercises.explanation: La contracción de 'they are' es 'they're'. Cuidado: no confundir con 'there' o 'their'.

exercises.question: My parents ___ doctors.
exercises.explanation: 'My parents' es plural → 'are'.

exercises.question: It ___ cold today.
exercises.explanation: 'It' es tercera persona singular → 'is'.

exercises.question: My mother's mother is my ___.
exercises.explanation: La madre de tu madre es tu abuela (grandmother).

exercises.question: I have one ___ and two ___.
exercises.explanation: Un familiar + plural: 'one sister and two brothers'. Los sustantivos plurales llevan -s.

exercises.question: This is my father's sister. She is my ___.
exercises.explanation: La hermana de tu padre o madre es tu tía (aunt).

exercises.question: ___ sister is a nurse.
exercises.explanation: Para indicar posesión se agrega 's al nombre: Carlos's sister. El apóstrofe va antes de la s.

exercises.question: My brother ___ fifteen years old.
exercises.explanation: Para la edad se usa 'to be': My brother IS fifteen years old.

exercises.question: His ___ name is Roberto.
exercises.explanation: Posesivo: father's (con apóstrofe + s) indica que el nombre le pertenece al padre.

exercises.question: My uncle's children are my ___.
exercises.explanation: Los hijos de tus tíos son tus primos (cousins).

exercises.question: I have two brothers ___ one sister.
exercises.explanation: Para unir elementos de una lista se usa 'and'.

exercises.question: My mother is a teacher. ___ is very smart.
exercises.explanation: Se usa 'she' para referirse a una mujer (mother).

exercises.question: My parents ___ from Spain.
exercises.explanation: 'My parents' = plural → 'are'.

exercises.question: She is ___ engineer.
exercises.explanation: 'Engineer' empieza con vocal /e/, entonces se usa 'an'.

exercises.question: He is ___ doctor.
exercises.explanation: 'Doctor' empieza con consonante /d/, entonces se usa 'a'.

exercises.question: 'What do you do?' means:
exercises.explanation: 'What do you do?' en inglés pregunta por la profesión u ocupación habitual.

exercises.question: She is ___ artist.
exercises.explanation: 'Artist' empieza con vocal /a/, entonces se usa 'an'.

exercises.question: He is ___ nurse.
exercises.explanation: 'Nurse' empieza con el sonido /n/ (consonante), entonces se usa 'a', no 'an'.

exercises.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
exercises.explanation: Las profesiones con 'to be' necesitan artículo (a/an). 'Engineer' empieza con vocal → 'an'.

exercises.question: He is ___ actor.
exercises.explanation: 'Actor' empieza con vocal /a/, entonces se usa 'an'.

exercises.question: 'I am a student.' What does the student answer to 'What do you do?'
exercises.explanation: Para dar la profesión/ocupación: I am + a/an + profesión.

exercises.question: She is ___ police officer.
exercises.explanation: 'Police officer' empieza con el sonido /p/ (consonante), entonces se usa 'a'.

exercises.question: He is ___ architect.
exercises.explanation: 'Architect' empieza con vocal /a/, entonces se usa 'an'.

exercises.question: She is from Argentina. She is ___.
exercises.explanation: El gentilicio de Argentina es 'Argentine' (o 'Argentinian'). No se usa 'Argentino'.

exercises.question: 'Where are you from?' — I ___ from Mexico.
exercises.explanation: Con 'I' se usa 'am'. La respuesta es: 'I am from Mexico'.

exercises.question: He is from France. He is ___.
exercises.explanation: El gentilicio de France es 'French'. No se agrega -an o -ish al nombre del país.

exercises.question: She speaks ___. (idioma de Brasil)
exercises.explanation: En Brasil se habla portugués (Portuguese), no 'Brazilian'.

exercises.question: He is from Japan. He is ___ and he speaks ___.
exercises.explanation: Tanto el gentilicio como el idioma de Japón son 'Japanese'.

exercises.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
exercises.explanation: Para el origen se usa 'from + nombre del país'. Los países llevan mayúscula.

exercises.question: He likes ___ food. (comida de Italia)
exercises.explanation: Los gentilicios usados como adjetivos: Italian food, French cinema, Spanish music.

exercises.question: She is from China. She is ___.
exercises.explanation: El gentilicio de China es 'Chinese'. Termina en -ese, como Japanese.

exercises.question: They are ___ Spain.
exercises.explanation: Para expresar origen se usa 'from': They are from Spain.

exercises.question: He is from Mexico. He speaks ___.
exercises.explanation: En México se habla español (Spanish). El idioma no es el mismo que el gentilicio.

exercises.question: ___ you a student?
exercises.explanation: Con 'you' se usa 'are'. En preguntas se invierte el orden: Are + you + ...?

exercises.question: Is she a teacher? — Yes, ___.
exercises.explanation: Las respuestas cortas afirmativas con 'to be' NO se contraen: 'Yes, she is'.

exercises.question: Are they from Italy? — No, ___.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta negativa con 'are': 'No, they aren't'. (aren't = are not)

exercises.question: She ___ a doctor. (negativo)
exercises.explanation: Negativo de 'she is': 'she isn't'. (isn't = is not)

exercises.question: ___ your brother at home?
exercises.explanation: 'Your brother' = tercera persona singular → pregunta con 'Is'.

exercises.question: They ___ students. (negativo)
exercises.explanation: Negativo de 'they are': 'they aren't'. (aren't = are not)

exercises.question: ___ your parents teachers?
exercises.explanation: 'Your parents' = plural → pregunta con 'Are'.

exercises.question: Is he from Spain? — No, ___ from Italy.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta negativa: 'No, he isn't'. También es correcto 'No, he's not'.

exercises.question: Which is the CORRECT question?
exercises.explanation: Para hacer preguntas con 'to be' se invierte el verbo y el sujeto: Is + she + a nurse?

exercises.question: ___ I late? — No, you ___ not.
exercises.explanation: Pregunta: 'Am I late?' Respuesta: 'No, you are not.' (o 'you aren't').

exercises.question: ___ name is Carlos.
exercises.explanation: 'My' es el adjetivo posesivo de 'I'. Va antes del sustantivo: My name.

exercises.question: The boy loves ___ dog.
exercises.explanation: 'His' se usa para masculino. No confundir con 'her' (femenino).

exercises.question: The girl loves ___ cat.
exercises.explanation: 'Her' se usa para femenino. Referimos a la niña (girl).

exercises.question: We live in a big house. ___ house has a garden.
exercises.explanation: 'Our' es el posesivo de 'we'. Hablamos de 'nosotros'.

exercises.question: The dog lost ___ collar.
exercises.explanation: 'Its' se usa para animales o cosas (sin apóstrofe). No confundir con 'it's' (it is).

exercises.question: The students have ___ books.
exercises.explanation: 'Their' es el posesivo de 'they'. Se usa para plural.

exercises.question: Is this ___ book? (hablando con alguien)
exercises.explanation: 'Your' es el posesivo de 'you'. Se usa al dirigirse directamente a alguien.

exercises.question: ___ parents are from Spain.
exercises.explanation: 'Their' = posesivo de ellos/ellas. No confundir con 'they' (pronombre) o 'there' (allá).

exercises.question: Maria is a doctor. ___ sister is a teacher.
exercises.explanation: Maria es femenina → posesivo 'her'. 'Her sister' = la hermana de ella.

exercises.question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
exercises.explanation: 'It's' (con apóstrofe) = it is. 'Its' (sin apóstrofe) = posesivo.

exercises.question: I am ___ home.
exercises.explanation: 'At home' es una expresión fija. Se usa 'at' con lugares puntuales: at home, at school, at work.

exercises.question: The keys are ___ the table.
exercises.explanation: 'On' = sobre la superficie. Las llaves están encima de la mesa.

exercises.question: The cat is ___ the box.
exercises.explanation: 'In' = dentro de un espacio cerrado. El gato está dentro de la caja.

exercises.question: The school is ___ the park and the hospital.
exercises.explanation: 'Between' se usa cuando algo está en el medio de dos cosas específicas.

exercises.question: She is ___ school now.
exercises.explanation: 'At school' es expresión fija. Se usa 'at' con los lugares de actividad: at school, at work, at the gym.

exercises.question: The supermarket is ___ the pharmacy. (al lado)
exercises.explanation: 'Next to' = justo al lado de algo. 'Near' es más general (cerca de).

exercises.question: The library is ___ the street. (justo enfrente)
exercises.explanation: 'Opposite' = enfrente (cruzando la calle).

exercises.question: The bus stop is ___ the corner.
exercises.explanation: 'At the corner' = en la esquina. Se usa 'at' para puntos de referencia específicos.

exercises.question: We live ___ a small town ___ the mountains.
exercises.explanation: 'In a town' (dentro de un lugar) + 'in the mountains' (en una zona geográfica).

exercises.question: The cinema is ___ the hotel. (detrás)
exercises.explanation: 'Behind' = detrás de. 'In front of' = delante de.

exercises.question: ___ a park near my house.
exercises.explanation: 'There is' + singular. Un parque (a park) es singular.

exercises.question: ___ two schools in my street.
exercises.explanation: 'There are' + plural. Dos escuelas (two schools) es plural.

exercises.question: ___ a supermarket near here? — Yes, there is.
exercises.explanation: Para hacer preguntas con 'there is' se invierte: 'Is there...?'

exercises.question: There ___ any buses on Sunday.
exercises.explanation: 'Buses' es plural → negativo: 'there aren't'. (aren't = are not)

exercises.question: ___ any good restaurants here?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con plural: 'Are there...?' → 'Are there any restaurants?'

exercises.question: There isn't ___ hospital in the village.
exercises.explanation: Con sustantivos singulares en negativo se usa 'a': 'There isn't a hospital'.

exercises.question: How many schools ___ in your city?
exercises.explanation: 'How many' + plural → 'are there'. El orden de pregunta: 'How many schools are there?'

exercises.question: There ___ a cinema, two restaurants and a park.
exercises.explanation: Cuando hay una lista, 'there is/are' concuerda con el PRIMER elemento: 'a cinema' (singular) → 'there is'.

exercises.question: ___ five students in the classroom.
exercises.explanation: 'Five students' es plural → 'There are five students'.

exercises.question: Is there a bus stop near here? — No, ___ .
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta negativa: 'No, there isn't'. Singular → isn't.

exercises.question: I always ___ at seven o'clock.
exercises.explanation: Con 'I' en presente simple el verbo no lleva -s: 'I wake up'.

exercises.question: She ___ to school every day.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: 'go' → 'goes' (se agrega -es porque termina en -o).

exercises.question: I have breakfast ___ the morning.
exercises.explanation: 'In the morning/afternoon/evening' son expresiones fijas. 'At night' es la excepción.

exercises.question: He ___ TV after dinner.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona: 'watch' → 'watches' (se agrega -es cuando termina en -ch).

exercises.question: We ___ lunch at school.
exercises.explanation: 'Have lunch' = almorzar. Con 'we' no se agrega -s.

exercises.question: She ___ goes to bed late. Choose the adverb that makes this sentence true: 'She goes to bed at 11pm every night without exception.'
exercises.explanation: 'Always' = siempre (el 100% de las veces). Va antes del verbo principal.

exercises.question: I ___ up at six thirty.
exercises.explanation: 'Get up' = levantarse. Con 'I' en presente simple no lleva -s.

exercises.question: She ___ home at five o'clock.
exercises.explanation: 'Come home' = llegar a casa. Tercera persona: 'comes'.

exercises.question: They ___ dinner at eight.
exercises.explanation: 'Have dinner' = cenar. Con 'they' no se agrega -s.

exercises.question: He ___ to bed at eleven.
exercises.explanation: 'Go to bed' = irse a la cama. Tercera persona: 'go' → 'goes'.

exercises.question: It's 3:00. How do you say it?
exercises.explanation: Para las horas en punto se dice 'three o'clock'. No se dice 'three hours'.

exercises.question: It's 2:30. How do you say it?
exercises.explanation: 2:30 = 'half past two'. 'Half past' + hora indica los 30 minutos.

exercises.question: It's 4:15. How do you say it?
exercises.explanation: 4:15 = 'quarter past four'. 'Quarter past' = 15 minutos después de la hora.

exercises.question: It's 4:45. How do you say it?
exercises.explanation: 4:45 = 'quarter to five'. 'Quarter to' = 15 minutos antes de la próxima hora.

exercises.question: I wake up ___ seven o'clock.
exercises.explanation: Para decir a qué hora se hace algo se usa 'at': 'at seven o'clock', 'at half past eight'.

exercises.question: How do you ask for the time?
exercises.explanation: La pregunta correcta es 'What time is it?' En español sería '¿Qué hora es?'.

exercises.question: It's 7:00. The class starts ___ seven o'clock.
exercises.explanation: Siempre 'at + hora exacta': at seven o'clock, at half past three.

exercises.question: It's 6:30. How do you say it?
exercises.explanation: 6:30 = 'half past six'. Se dice la hora actual + 'half past'.

exercises.question: It's 9:15. How do you say it?
exercises.explanation: 9:15 = 'quarter past nine'. 15 minutos después de las 9.

exercises.question: School finishes ___ half past three.
exercises.explanation: 'At' se usa siempre con horas específicas: at half past three, at quarter to four.

exercises.question: She ___ to school every day.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: 'go' → 'goes'. Los verbos terminados en -o añaden -es.

exercises.question: He ___ TV at night.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona: 'watch' → 'watches'. Los verbos en -ch/-sh/-x/-o añaden -es.

exercises.question: I ___ in a big city.
exercises.explanation: Con 'I' el verbo no cambia: 'I live' (sin -s).

exercises.question: She ___ three languages.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona: se agrega -s al verbo. 'speak' → 'speaks'.

exercises.question: My parents ___ in Buenos Aires.
exercises.explanation: 'My parents' es plural → verbo sin -s: 'live'.

exercises.question: She ___ lunch at school.
exercises.explanation: 'Have' es irregular en tercera persona: 'has', no 'haves'.

exercises.question: He ___ a lot of homework.
exercises.explanation: 'Do' es irregular en tercera persona: 'does', no 'dos' ni 'doos'.

exercises.question: They ___ to the gym on Mondays.
exercises.explanation: 'They' es plural → verbo sin -s: 'go'.

exercises.question: She ___ early every morning.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona + phrasal verb: 'wakes up'. La -s va en el verbo principal.

exercises.question: He ___ chess with his grandfather.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona: 'play' → 'plays'. Verbos que terminan en vocal + consonante solo añaden -s.

exercises.question: My sister ___ long hair.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona (my sister) → 'has got'.

exercises.question: We ___ a car.
exercises.explanation: Negativo con 'we': 'haven't got'. (we = I/you/we/they → have)

exercises.question: ___ your brother got a bike?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'have got' en tercera persona: 'Has + he/she/it + got...?'

exercises.question: ___ they got any pets?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'have got': 'Have + they + got...?'

exercises.question: She has got ___ eyes. (azules)
exercises.explanation: Los adjetivos de color no van con artículo ni llevan -s: 'blue eyes'.

exercises.question: Has he got a dog? — Yes, ___.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta a 'Has he got...?' → 'Yes, he has'.

exercises.question: My parents ___ a house in the country.
exercises.explanation: 'My parents' = plural → 'have got'.

exercises.question: I ___ short hair.
exercises.explanation: Con 'I' → 'have got'. Para describir apariencia física.

exercises.question: She hasn't got a car. ___ she got a bike?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta en tercera persona con 'have got': 'Has she got...?'

exercises.question: My grandfather ___ a big garden.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular (my grandfather) → 'has got'.

exercises.question: He has got brown ___.
exercises.explanation: Se tienen dos ojos (plural): 'brown eyes'. No se usa artículo.

exercises.question: I haven't got ___ brothers.
exercises.explanation: En negativas e interrogativas se usa 'any': 'I haven't got any brothers'.

exercises.question: Have you got any pets? — No, I ___ .
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta negativa a 'Have you got...?' → 'No, I haven't'.

exercises.question: She has got ___ hair. (corto)
exercises.explanation: Los adjetivos van sin artículo cuando describen el sustantivo directamente: 'short hair'.

exercises.question: They ___ any money.
exercises.explanation: 'They' usa 'haven't got' en negativo.

exercises.question: My cousin has got a ___ face. (redonda)
exercises.explanation: Adjetivo antes de sustantivo, sin artículo adicional: 'a round face'.

exercises.question: Has she got curly hair? — No, she ___ straight hair.
exercises.explanation: La respuesta describe lo que SÍ tiene. Tercera persona → 'has got'.

exercises.question: We have got ___ cousins. (muchos)
exercises.explanation: 'A lot of' = muchos/as. Se usa con sustantivos contables e incontables.

exercises.question: My brother hasn't got ___ . (ninguna mascota)
exercises.explanation: 'Any' se usa en oraciones negativas: 'He hasn't got any pets'.

exercises.question: Have your parents got a big house? — Yes, they ___ .
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta a 'Have they got...?' → 'Yes, they have'.

exercises.question: My father ___ speak three languages.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' nunca cambia con la persona. 'My father can speak...' es correcto.

exercises.question: She ___ dance really well.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' no cambia, incluso en tercera persona. No hay -s ni 'to'.

exercises.question: ___ you play chess?
exercises.explanation: Para habilidades se pregunta con 'Can + sujeto + verbo?'

exercises.question: They ___ ride a horse.
exercises.explanation: Negativo de 'can': 'can't'. No se usa 'don't' ni 'doesn't' con 'can'.

exercises.question: Can I open the window? — ___, of course.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta a 'Can I...?' → 'Yes, you can' (permiso).

exercises.question: You ___ park here. (está prohibido)
exercises.explanation: 'Can't' se usa para prohibición o falta de permiso: 'You can't park here'.

exercises.question: Can he cook? — No, but he ___ make sandwiches.
exercises.explanation: 'He can make sandwiches' = afirmativo. 'Can' sin -s ni 'to'.

exercises.question: My sister ___ play the guitar but she ___ sing.
exercises.explanation: Contraste: sí puede tocar, no puede cantar → 'can / can't'.

exercises.question: ___ your sister swim?
exercises.explanation: Para preguntar sobre habilidades se usa 'Can + sujeto + verbo?'

exercises.question: He can't speak French, but he ___ speak English.
exercises.explanation: Contraste de habilidades. Afirmativo: 'he can speak English'.

exercises.question: We ___ play chess very well.
exercises.explanation: Con 'we', 'can' tampoco cambia: 'We can play chess'.

exercises.question: Can your dog do tricks? — No, it ___ .
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta negativa: 'No, it can't'.

exercises.question: They ___ speak Chinese. (no pueden)
exercises.explanation: Negativo de 'can' para cualquier persona: 'can't'.

exercises.question: ___ she run fast?
exercises.explanation: Preguntas sobre habilidades: 'Can + she + verbo?'

exercises.question: I ___ ride a bike but I ___ drive a car.
exercises.explanation: Puede andar en bici (can) pero no puede manejar (can't).

exercises.question: Is ___ your book or that one?
exercises.explanation: Comparando un objeto cercano (this) con uno lejano (that). Singular.

exercises.question: ___ your keys? (cerca, varias llaves)
exercises.explanation: 'Keys' es plural y están cerca → 'Are these your keys?'

exercises.question: How much is ___? (señalando un libro cercano)
exercises.explanation: Señalando un objeto cercano y singular → 'this'. '¿Cuánto cuesta esto?'

exercises.question: ___ shoes are expensive! (los de allá, varios)
exercises.explanation: Zapatos (plural) + lejos → 'those'.

exercises.question: This is my friend Maria. — ___ to meet you.
exercises.explanation: Al presentar a alguien, la respuesta es 'Nice to meet you'.

exercises.question: Is ___ the right bus? (el que está acá)
exercises.explanation: Singular + cerca → 'this'.

exercises.question: ___ are my parents. (presentando a alguien cercano)
exercises.explanation: Para presentar a varias personas que están cerca → 'These are my parents'.

exercises.question: Look at ___ mountains! (lejos, varias)
exercises.explanation: Plural + lejos → 'those'. '¡Mira esas montañas!'.

exercises.question: ___ is my school. (señalando un edificio lejos)
exercises.explanation: Singular + lejos → 'that'.

exercises.question: Are ___ your glasses? (las que están en la mesa cerca tuyo)
exercises.explanation: Plural + cerca → 'these'. '¿Son estos tus anteojos?'

exercises.question: The museum is ___ the park. (justo enfrente)
exercises.explanation: 'Opposite' = enfrente (al otro lado de la calle).

exercises.question: Turn left ___ the traffic lights.
exercises.explanation: 'At the traffic lights / at the corner' — se usa 'at' para puntos de referencia en indicaciones.

exercises.question: The pharmacy is ___ the first floor.
exercises.explanation: Para pisos de un edificio se usa 'on': 'on the first floor', 'on the ground floor'.

exercises.question: The station is ___ from here. (lejos)
exercises.explanation: 'Far from here' = lejos de aquí. 'Close to' = cerca de.

exercises.question: The hotel is ___ two big buildings.
exercises.explanation: 'Between' = entre dos cosas. 'The hotel is between two buildings'.

exercises.question: Go straight ___ and turn right.
exercises.explanation: 'Go straight ahead' = sigue derecho. 'On' no se usa así en indicaciones.

exercises.question: The park is ___ to the station. (cerca)
exercises.explanation: 'Close to' = cerca de. También se puede decir 'near the station' (sin 'to').

exercises.question: The supermarket is ___ the school. (detrás)
exercises.explanation: 'Behind' = detrás de. 'In front of' = delante de.

exercises.question: My house is ___ the city center. (lejos)
exercises.explanation: 'Far from + lugar' = lejos de un lugar.

exercises.question: The bus stop is ___ the corner.
exercises.explanation: 'At the corner' = en la esquina. 'At' se usa para puntos de referencia específicos.

exercises.question: My brother ___ vegetables.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona negativo: 'doesn't like'. El verbo va SIN -s.

exercises.question: ___ she like pop music?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta en tercera persona: 'Does + she + like?' (sin -s en el verbo).

exercises.question: What kind of food ___ you like?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'you': 'What kind of food do you like?'

exercises.question: I ___ Italian food. It's delicious!
exercises.explanation: Con 'I' el verbo no lleva -s: 'I like Italian food'.

exercises.question: Does your sister like sports? — No, she ___.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta: se repite el auxiliar 'does' en negativo → 'No, she doesn't'.

exercises.question: Go straight ___ and turn left at the lights.
exercises.explanation: 'Go straight ahead' = sigue recto. Es la expresión fija.

exercises.question: ___ right at the traffic lights.
exercises.explanation: 'Turn left/right' = girar. Con 'go' se dice 'go straight'.

exercises.question: Take the ___ road on the left.
exercises.explanation: 'Take the first/second road on the left/right' = toma la primera/segunda calle a la izquierda/derecha.

exercises.question: ___ much is a coffee here?
exercises.explanation: Para preguntar precios: 'How much is / does ... cost?'

exercises.question: The ticket ___ three pounds.
exercises.explanation: 'It costs £3' = cuesta £3. También 'It is £3' es correcto pero 'costs' es más natural aquí.

exercises.question: The hotel ___ a gym and a swimming pool.
exercises.explanation: El hotel (singular, tercera persona) usa 'has got'.

exercises.question: The museum ___ open today.
exercises.explanation: Para describir estados (abierto/cerrado) se usa 'to be': 'is/isn't open'.

exercises.question: Go ___ ahead and take the first left. (sigue recto)
exercises.explanation: 'Go straight ahead' = seguir recto.

exercises.question: How much ___ the sandwiches cost? (verbo correcto para plural)
exercises.explanation: Para plural: 'How much do the sandwiches cost?'

exercises.question: The café ___ got a terrace with great views. (verbo)
exercises.explanation: El café (singular) → 'has got'.

exercises.question: Take the left on first road.
exercises.answer: Take the first road on the left.
exercises.explanation: El orden correcto es: 'Take the first/second road on the left/right'.

exercises.question: How many is the coffee?
exercises.explanation: Para preguntar precios: 'How much', no 'how many'.

exercises.question: The museum have got two cafés.
exercises.answer: The museum has got two cafés.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: 'has got', no 'have got'.

exercises.question: The bank is in front the park.
exercises.answer: The bank is in front of the park.
exercises.explanation: 'In front of' siempre lleva 'of'. No se puede omitir.

exercises.question: Excuse me, ___ is the ticket for the zoo?
exercises.explanation: 'How much is the ticket?' = ¿Cuánto cuesta la entrada? Se usa 'how much' para precios.

exercises.question: She ___ ride a motorbike but she has never tried.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' + infinitivo sin 'to'. Nunca cambia con la persona.

exercises.question: I ___ turn on the computer. Can you help me?
exercises.explanation: Negativo de 'can' = 'can't'. Nunca con 'don't'.

exercises.question: She ___ a new smartphone with a great camera.
exercises.explanation: She (tercera persona) → 'has got'.

exercises.question: I ___ a charger. Can I borrow yours?
exercises.explanation: I (primera persona) negativo → 'haven't got'.

exercises.question: Can your sister speak French? — Yes, _____.
exercises.explanation: Respuesta corta con 'can': sujeto + 'can' (sin verbo extra).

exercises.question: How much money ___ you got?
exercises.explanation: 'Have you got...?' = ¿Tienes...? Con 'have got' la pregunta se forma moviendo 'have'.

exercises.question: ___ you ride a bicycle? (pregunta)
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'can': 'Can + sujeto + infinitivo?'

exercises.question: I ___ got a webcam for video calls. (negativo)
exercises.explanation: 'I haven't got' = no tengo.

exercises.question: My little brother ___ read yet but he can draw very well.
exercises.explanation: 'Can't' = negativo de 'can'.

exercises.question: Has she ___ a laptop at home?
exercises.explanation: 'Has she got...?' = ¿Tiene ella...?

exercises.question: He can to use a computer very well.
exercises.answer: He can use a computer very well.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'can' el verbo va en infinitivo SIN 'to'.

exercises.question: She hasn't got no internet at home.
exercises.answer: She hasn't got any internet at home.
exercises.explanation: En inglés no hay doble negativo. Con 'hasn't got' se usa 'any', no 'no'.

exercises.question: Does he can drive?
exercises.explanation: No se usa 'does' con 'can'. La pregunta es 'Can + sujeto + infinitivo?'

exercises.question: I have got not a tablet.
exercises.explanation: El negativo de 'have got' es 'haven't got'.

exercises.question: She cans speak three languages.
exercises.explanation: 'Can' NUNCA lleva -s, ni siquiera en tercera persona.

exercises.question: I love ___. I go every Saturday morning.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'love/like/hate' usamos gerundio (-ing) o infinitivo con 'to'. 'Swim' solo (sin -ing ni to) no es correcto.

exercises.question: She hates ___ up early in the morning.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'hate' se usa gerundio (-ing) o infinitivo. 'Getting up' es el gerundio.

exercises.question: He ___ eats meat. He is a vegetarian.
exercises.explanation: Si es vegetariano, 'never' (nunca) es la respuesta lógica y correcta.

exercises.question: I ___ have cereal for breakfast. I eat it every single morning.
exercises.explanation: 'Always' = siempre, el 100% del tiempo.

exercises.question: Do you enjoy ___? I love going to new places.
exercises.explanation: 'Enjoy' siempre va seguido de gerundio (-ing). No se usa infinitivo con 'to'.

exercises.question: She ___ goes to the gym. About once or twice a year.
exercises.explanation: 'Rarely' = casi nunca. 'Sometimes' = a veces. 'Usually' = normalmente.

exercises.question: I ___ eat fast food. Maybe once a month. (a veces)
exercises.explanation: 'Sometimes' = a veces. Va normalmente antes del verbo principal.

exercises.question: She ___ goes swimming twice a week. (normalmente)
exercises.explanation: 'Usually' = normalmente. Frecuencia alta pero no siempre.

exercises.question: My brother enjoys ___ video games in his free time.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'enjoy' siempre va el gerundio (-ing).

exercises.question: I ___ miss breakfast. I eat it every day. (nunca)
exercises.explanation: 'Never' = nunca. Va antes del verbo principal.

exercises.question: She enjoy cooking for her family.
exercises.answer: She enjoys cooking for her family.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: 'enjoys' (con -s). Además, 'enjoy' + gerundio.

exercises.question: He goes always to the gym on Mondays.
exercises.answer: He always goes to the gym on Mondays.
exercises.explanation: Los adverbios de frecuencia van ANTES del verbo principal: 'always goes', no 'goes always'.

exercises.question: I love go to the cinema on Fridays.
exercises.answer: I love going to the cinema on Fridays.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'love' se usa gerundio (-ing) o infinitivo con 'to'. 'Go' solo no es correcto.

exercises.question: She sometimes is late for class.
exercises.answer: She is sometimes late for class.
exercises.explanation: Con 'to be', el adverbio de frecuencia va DESPUÉS del verbo: 'is sometimes', no 'sometimes is'.

exercises.question: They doesn't like spicy food at all.
exercises.answer: They don't like spicy food at all.
exercises.explanation: Con 'they' el negativo es 'don't', no 'doesn't'.

exercises.question: I _____ Japan twice.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect para hablar de experiencias de vida sin tiempo específico.

exercises.question: _____ you ever been to South America?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con present perfect: Have/Has + sujeto + past participle.

exercises.question: She _____ never tried sushi.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular (she) usa 'has' en el present perfect.

exercises.question: We _____ just arrived at the airport.
exercises.explanation: 'Just' con present perfect indica una acción reciente.

exercises.question: He _____ already booked the hotel.
exercises.explanation: 'Already' con present perfect: la acción se completó antes de lo esperado.

exercises.question: I _____ (visit) ten countries so far.
exercises.explanation: 'So far' (hasta ahora) indica present perfect: have + past participle.

exercises.question: She _____ (never / go) to Europe.
exercises.explanation: Para 'go' con 'been to' = haber estado en un lugar.

exercises.question: _____ they _____ (book) the flights yet?
exercises.explanation: 'Yet' en preguntas = ¿ya...? Se usa con present perfect.

exercises.question: I have went to Paris last year.
exercises.answer: I went to Paris last year.
exercises.explanation: Con tiempo específico (last year), se usa simple past, no present perfect.

exercises.question: Have you ever went abroad?
exercises.explanation: El participio de 'go' es 'been' cuando indica experiencia de visitar un lugar.

exercises.question: Tokyo is _____ than I expected.
exercises.explanation: Adjetivos cortos (1 sílaba): comparativo con -er (big → bigger).

exercises.question: This hotel is _____ comfortable than the last one.
exercises.explanation: Adjetivos largos (más de 2 sílabas): comparativo con 'more'.

exercises.question: This is _____ trip I have ever taken.
exercises.explanation: Superlativo de adjetivos largos: the most + adjetivo.

exercises.question: Travelling by train is _____ than flying.
exercises.explanation: Adjetivos cortos forman el comparativo con -er.

exercises.question: Which is _____ city in the world?
exercises.explanation: Superlativo: the + most + adjetivo largo.

exercises.question: Paris is _____ (beautiful) than I thought.
exercises.explanation: Comparativo de adjetivo largo: more + adjetivo.

exercises.question: This is _____ (good) hotel in the city.
exercises.explanation: Superlativo irregular: good → the best.

exercises.question: The hostel is _____ (cheap) than the hotel.
exercises.explanation: Comparativo de adjetivo corto: cheap → cheaper.

exercises.question: Rome is more older than Paris.
exercises.explanation: No se combina 'more' con adjetivos cortos (-er). Elige uno: 'older' o 'more old'.

exercises.question: It was the most best trip of my life.
exercises.answer: It was the best trip of my life.
exercises.explanation: Los superlativos irregulares (best, worst) no llevan 'most'.

exercises.question: We _____ visit the Colosseum tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' para planes decididos previamente.

exercises.question: Look at those clouds. It _____ rain!
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' para predicciones basadas en evidencia visible.

exercises.question: They _____ take the night train.
exercises.explanation: Con 'they' (plural), el auxiliar es 'are going to'.

exercises.question: _____ you _____ rent a car?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'going to': Are/Is/Am + sujeto + going to + verbo.

exercises.question: She _____ not going to miss her flight this time.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: 'she is going to' (negativo: is not going to).

exercises.question: I _____ (take) a lot of photos on this trip.
exercises.explanation: Plan decidido: am/is/are + going to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: We _____ (not / fly). We prefer the train.
exercises.explanation: Negativo de going to: am/is/are + not + going to + verbo.

exercises.question: He _____ (spend) two weeks in Thailand.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona singular: is going to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: I going to visit the museum.
exercises.answer: I am going to visit the museum.
exercises.explanation: Se necesita el auxiliar 'am/is/are' antes de 'going to'.

exercises.question: They are going visit the castle.
exercises.answer: They are going to visit the castle.
exercises.explanation: No olvidar el 'to' entre 'going' y el verbo: going to visit.

exercises.question: You _____ book your tickets in advance.
exercises.explanation: 'Should' para dar consejos o recomendaciones.

exercises.question: Travellers _____ respect local customs.
exercises.explanation: 'Should' expresa una obligación moral o recomendación.

exercises.question: You _____ forget your passport!
exercises.explanation: 'Shouldn't' (should not) para aconsejar en contra de algo.

exercises.question: _____ I take an umbrella?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'should': se invierte el orden Should + sujeto.

exercises.question: You _____ arrive early to check in.
exercises.explanation: 'Ought to' tiene el mismo significado que 'should' pero lleva 'to'.

exercises.question: You _____ (try) the local food — it's amazing!
exercises.explanation: should + infinitivo sin 'to' para recomendaciones.

exercises.question: We _____ (not / leave) our bags unattended.
exercises.explanation: Consejo negativo: shouldn't + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Tourists _____ (respect) the local culture.
exercises.explanation: 'Should' + infinitivo para obligaciones morales.

exercises.question: You should to visit the old town.
exercises.answer: You should visit the old town.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'should' NO va 'to'. Solo: should + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Should I to bring cash?
exercises.explanation: 'Should' es modal: no usa 'to' antes del infinitivo.

exercises.question: The flight was delayed, _____?
exercises.explanation: Con 'was' positivo, el tag es negativo: wasn't it.

exercises.question: You haven't been here before, _____?
exercises.explanation: Con present perfect negativo, el tag es positivo.

exercises.question: They're going to Paris, _____?
exercises.explanation: Con 'are' positivo, el tag es negativo: aren't they.

exercises.question: She speaks French, _____?
exercises.explanation: Presente simple afirmativo → tag negativo con 'doesn't'.

exercises.question: You won't forget to call, _____?
exercises.explanation: 'Won't' negativo → tag positivo 'will you'.

exercises.question: It's a beautiful city, _____?
exercises.explanation: 'It's' (is positivo) → tag negativo: isn't it.

exercises.question: You can speak Japanese, _____?
exercises.explanation: 'Can' positivo → tag negativo: can't you.

exercises.question: They didn't miss the train, _____?
exercises.explanation: 'Didn't' negativo → tag positivo: did they.

exercises.question: She's from Italy, isn't she is?
exercises.explanation: Los question tags son cortos: solo auxiliar + pronombre.

exercises.question: You booked the hotel, did you?
exercises.answer: You booked the hotel, didn't you?
exercises.explanation: Oración positiva → tag negativo. 'Booked' (simple past afirmativo) → didn't you.

exercises.question: I _____ in this company for five years.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect con 'for' + período de tiempo (situación que continúa).

exercises.question: She _____ just been promoted to manager.
exercises.explanation: 'Just' con present perfect (tercera persona: has).

exercises.question: How long _____ you worked here?
exercises.explanation: 'How long' pregunta la duración: How long + have/has + sujeto + past participle.

exercises.question: I _____ met the new director yet.
exercises.explanation: 'Yet' en negativo: haven't/hasn't + past participle + yet.

exercises.question: He has worked here _____ 2019.
exercises.explanation: 'Since' + punto de inicio (año, fecha); 'for' + período de duración.

exercises.question: They _____ (not / receive) my CV yet.
exercises.explanation: Negativo present perfect: haven't/hasn't + past participle.

exercises.question: She _____ (work) as a nurse for ten years.
exercises.explanation: 'For' + período: presente perfect indica una acción que comenzó antes y continúa.

exercises.question: I _____ (already / send) my application.
exercises.explanation: 'Already' con present perfect: acción completada antes de lo esperado.

exercises.question: I have worked here since five years.
exercises.answer: I have worked here for five years.
exercises.explanation: 'For' + período de tiempo (five years); 'since' + punto en el tiempo (since 2019).

exercises.question: Did you ever work abroad?
exercises.explanation: 'Ever' con experiencias de vida usa present perfect, no simple past.

exercises.question: If I _____ the manager, I would give everyone a pay rise.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: If + were (formal/correcto) o was. La cláusula principal usa 'would'.

exercises.question: I would apply for that job if I _____ more experience.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: If + simple past (had). La situación es hipotética.

exercises.question: If she _____ the interview, she would get the job.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula con 'if' en segundo condicional: simple past.

exercises.question: He _____ resign if the boss treated him better.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula principal del segundo condicional: would/wouldn't + infinitivo.

exercises.question: What _____ you do if you lost your job?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con segundo condicional: What would + sujeto + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If I _____ (be) you, I would ask for a raise.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: If I were you (consejo hipotético).

exercises.question: She _____ (work) from home if she could.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula principal: would + infinitivo (sin 'to').

exercises.question: If they _____ (offer) me the job, I would accept immediately.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if' en segundo condicional: simple past.

exercises.question: If I would have more time, I would learn a new skill.
exercises.answer: If I had more time, I would learn a new skill.
exercises.explanation: En la cláusula 'if' del segundo condicional NO se usa 'would'. Solo simple past.

exercises.question: If she was the boss, she will change everything.
exercises.answer: If she were the boss, she would change everything.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: if + were/was, + would (no 'will').

exercises.question: You _____ arrive late to a job interview.
exercises.explanation: 'Mustn't' = prohibición fuerte. 'Don't have to' = no es necesario (diferente).

exercises.question: She _____ wear a uniform at work.
exercises.explanation: Obligación externa (regla del trabajo): has to (tercera persona).

exercises.question: You _____ submit your report by Friday. It's the deadline.
exercises.explanation: 'Must' para obligación interna/importante. 'Have to' también sería correcto.

exercises.question: He _____ work on Sundays. It's not required.
exercises.explanation: 'Don't/doesn't have to' = no hay obligación (≠ mustn't que es prohibición).

exercises.question: Did you _____ take a test before getting the job?
exercises.explanation: Pasado de 'have to': did you have to (pasado simple del auxiliar 'do').

exercises.question: Employees _____ (sign) a contract before starting work.
exercises.explanation: Obligación externa (regla de la empresa): have to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: You _____ (not / share) your password with anyone.
exercises.explanation: 'Mustn't' para prohibición fuerte.

exercises.question: She _____ (not / work) overtime — it's optional.
exercises.explanation: 'Doesn't have to' = no es obligatorio.

exercises.question: You must to send your CV by tomorrow.
exercises.answer: You must send your CV by tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'must' NO va 'to'. Solo: must + infinitivo.

exercises.question: She musts arrive on time.
exercises.explanation: 'Must' nunca lleva -s. Es un modal y no cambia con la persona.

exercises.question: The report _____ by the team every month.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente: is/are + past participle.

exercises.question: She _____ last week.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva pasada: was/were + past participle.

exercises.question: All new employees _____ a training course.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente con sujeto plural: are + past participle.

exercises.question: The interview will _____ online.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de futuro (will): will + be + past participle.

exercises.question: He _____ for being late three times.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was/were + past participle.

exercises.question: The salaries _____ (increase) twice last year.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva pasado: were + past participle.

exercises.question: Applications _____ (accept) until the 30th.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente: are + past participle.

exercises.question: The new policy _____ (announce) at the meeting.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was + past participle.

exercises.question: The contract was sign last Monday.
exercises.answer: The contract was signed last Monday.
exercises.explanation: La voz pasiva requiere el past participle (signed), no el infinitivo.

exercises.question: The report is write by the manager.
exercises.answer: The report is written by the manager.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente: is + past participle (written, no write).

exercises.question: She said she _____ working from home.
exercises.explanation: Estilo indirecto: 'is' pasa a 'was' (backshift).

exercises.question: He told me he _____ apply for the promotion.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' pasa a 'would' en el estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: She said she _____ finished the report.
exercises.explanation: 'Has finished' (present perfect) pasa a 'had finished' (past perfect) en estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: He asked me where _____ working.
exercises.explanation: En preguntas indirectas, el orden es sujeto + verbo (no se invierte).

exercises.question: My boss told me _____ late again.
exercises.explanation: Reported command negativo: told + objeto + not to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Direct: 'I will send the email.' → She said she _____ send the email.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' pasa a 'would' en el estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: Direct: 'I work here.' → He said he _____ there.
exercises.explanation: Simple present pasa a simple past en el estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: Direct: 'Please send your CV.' → She asked me _____ my CV.
exercises.explanation: Reported request: asked + objeto + to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: He said me that he was tired.
exercises.answer: He told me that he was tired.
exercises.explanation: 'Tell' se usa con objeto (told me). 'Say' no lleva objeto directo de persona: he said (that)...

exercises.question: She asked where was I working.
exercises.answer: She asked where I was working.
exercises.explanation: En preguntas indirectas el orden es sujeto + verbo, no se invierte como en la pregunta directa.

exercises.question: You _____ eat more vegetables.
exercises.explanation: 'Should' para dar consejos de salud.

exercises.question: You _____ smoke — it's very harmful.
exercises.explanation: 'Shouldn't' para aconsejar no hacer algo.

exercises.question: The doctor said I _____ take the medication twice a day.
exercises.explanation: Consejo médico usando 'should'.

exercises.question: She _____ see a specialist for her back pain.
exercises.explanation: 'Ought to' = recomendación, equivalente a 'should' pero lleva 'to'.

exercises.question: You _____ stay in bed if you have a fever.
exercises.explanation: Consejo: should + infinitivo sin 'to'.

exercises.question: You _____ (drink) at least eight glasses of water a day.
exercises.explanation: Consejo de salud: should + infinitivo.

exercises.question: He _____ (not / eat) so much junk food.
exercises.explanation: Consejo negativo: shouldn't + infinitivo.

exercises.question: You _____ (see) a doctor about that cough.
exercises.explanation: Recomendación médica con 'should'.

exercises.question: You should to exercise more.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'should' NO va 'to'. Solo: should + infinitivo.

exercises.question: He oughts to take his medicine.
exercises.answer: He ought to take his medicine.
exercises.explanation: 'Ought' no lleva -s y es siempre seguido de 'to': ought to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If you _____ enough, you'll feel better.
exercises.explanation: Primer condicional: If + presente simple, will + infinitivo.

exercises.question: You'll lose weight if you _____ more.
exercises.explanation: La cláusula 'if' usa presente simple (no will) en el primer condicional.

exercises.question: If she doesn't take her medication, she _____ worse.
exercises.explanation: Resultado del primer condicional: will + infinitivo.

exercises.question: _____ you call an ambulance if someone collapses?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta en primer condicional: Will + sujeto + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If he _____ the operation, he'll recover quickly.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if' en primer condicional: presente simple.

exercises.question: If you _____ (not / drink) water, you'll get dehydrated.
exercises.explanation: Negativo del primer condicional: If + don't/doesn't + verbo.

exercises.question: She _____ (feel) better if she rests.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula resultado: will + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If you _____ (eat) well, you'll have more energy.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if': presente simple (no 'will eat').

exercises.question: If you will eat healthy, you'll feel better.
exercises.answer: If you eat healthy, you'll feel better.
exercises.explanation: En la cláusula 'if' del primer condicional NO se usa 'will'. Solo presente simple.

exercises.question: If she takes the medicine, she get better.
exercises.answer: If she takes the medicine, she will get better.
exercises.explanation: La cláusula resultado necesita 'will + infinitivo'.

exercises.question: I _____ smoke a pack a day, but I quit.
exercises.explanation: 'Used to' para hábitos del pasado que ya no ocurren.

exercises.question: She _____ eat a lot of fast food when she was young.
exercises.explanation: 'Used to + infinitivo' para estados o hábitos pasados.

exercises.question: He _____ exercise at all before his heart attack.
exercises.explanation: Negativo de 'used to': didn't use to (sin -d después de 'use').

exercises.question: _____ they use to eat meat before becoming vegetarian?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con 'used to': Did + sujeto + use to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: We _____ walk to school every day when we were kids.
exercises.explanation: 'Used to' para acciones habituales pasadas que ya no ocurren.

exercises.question: He _____ (be) overweight, but he changed his diet.
exercises.explanation: Estado pasado que cambió: used to + be.

exercises.question: I _____ (not / like) vegetables, but now I love them.
exercises.explanation: Negativo: didn't use to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: _____ she _____ (take) sleeping pills every night?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta: Did + sujeto + use to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: I use to go jogging every morning.
exercises.answer: I used to go jogging every morning.
exercises.explanation: En afirmativo es 'used to' (con -d). Solo pierde la -d en preguntas/negativo con 'did'.

exercises.question: Did she used to work night shifts?
exercises.answer: Did she use to work night shifts?
exercises.explanation: Con 'did', se pierde la -d: 'did she use to' (no 'used to').

exercises.question: It _____ be serious — you should see a doctor.
exercises.explanation: 'May/might' para expresar posibilidad (no certeza).

exercises.question: She _____ have an allergy — we're not sure yet.
exercises.explanation: 'Might' expresa posibilidad más débil que 'may'.

exercises.question: The test results _____ not be ready until tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: 'Might not' = posiblemente no.

exercises.question: You _____ feel dizzy after the medication.
exercises.explanation: 'May' para posible efecto secundario.

exercises.question: I'm not sure, but the appointment _____ be at 3 pm.
exercises.explanation: 'Might' para incertidumbre.

exercises.question: The doctor said it _____ (be) a viral infection.
exercises.explanation: Posibilidad: might + infinitivo.

exercises.question: She _____ (have) surgery if the medication doesn't work.
exercises.explanation: Posibilidad futura: may + infinitivo.

exercises.question: He _____ (not / recover) quickly — it depends on the treatment.
exercises.explanation: Posibilidad negativa: might not + infinitivo.

exercises.question: It mights be a serious illness.
exercises.answer: It might be a serious illness.
exercises.explanation: 'Might' es modal: NUNCA lleva -s.

exercises.question: She may to have an operation.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'may/might' NO va 'to'. Solo: may/might + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Thousands of trees _____ every year.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente plural: are + past participle.

exercises.question: The Amazon rainforest _____ at an alarming rate.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva continua presente: is/are being + past participle (acción en progreso).

exercises.question: Many species _____ due to habitat loss.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente plural: are + past participle.

exercises.question: New renewable energy plants _____ across the country.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva continua presente: are being + past participle.

exercises.question: The new environmental law _____ last month.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was/were + past participle.

exercises.question: Plastic waste _____ (dump) into the ocean every day.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente: is + past participle.

exercises.question: Thousands of animals _____ (kill) by pollution each year.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente plural: are + past participle.

exercises.question: The coral reef _____ (damage) by rising sea temperatures.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva continua: is being + past participle.

exercises.question: Forests is destroyed every day.
exercises.explanation: Sujeto plural (Forests) usa 'are', no 'is'.

exercises.question: The law was sign by the president.
exercises.answer: The law was signed by the president.
exercises.explanation: La voz pasiva necesita el past participle (signed), no el infinitivo.

exercises.question: The animal _____ is most affected by climate change is the polar bear.
exercises.explanation: 'Which' se usa para cosas/animales en cláusulas relativas.

exercises.question: Scientists _____ study climate change are very concerned.
exercises.explanation: 'Who' se usa para personas en cláusulas relativas.

exercises.question: This is the river _____ water has been contaminated.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' indica posesión en cláusulas relativas.

exercises.question: The country _____ I was born in has serious pollution problems.
exercises.explanation: 'Which' o 'that' para referirse a lugares/cosas.

exercises.question: The scientist _____ discovered this species won the Nobel Prize.
exercises.explanation: 'Who' para personas.

exercises.question: The forest _____ is being cut down is home to thousands of species.
exercises.explanation: 'Which' para cosas/lugares.

exercises.question: The activist _____ led the campaign was arrested.
exercises.explanation: 'Who' para personas.

exercises.question: The organisation _____ goal is to protect wildlife needs more funding.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' para indicar posesión.

exercises.question: The animal which it lives in the Arctic is the polar bear.
exercises.answer: The animal which lives in the Arctic is the polar bear.
exercises.explanation: En cláusulas relativas no se repite el pronombre sujeto (which ya es el sujeto, no se añade 'it').

exercises.question: The scientist what studied global warming won an award.
exercises.answer: The scientist who studied global warming won an award.
exercises.explanation: 'What' no se usa en cláusulas relativas. Para personas: 'who'; para cosas: 'which/that'.

exercises.question: If people _____ more, there would be less plastic waste.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: If + simple past (situación hipotética).

exercises.question: The planet _____ healthier if we used fewer fossil fuels.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: cláusula resultado usa 'would + infinitivo'.

exercises.question: If governments _____ more, climate change could be slowed.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if' del segundo condicional: simple past.

exercises.question: More species _____ survive if habitats were protected.
exercises.explanation: Resultado hipotético: would/could + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If I _____ a politician, I would create stronger environmental laws.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: If + was/were (ambos son aceptables).

exercises.question: If we _____ (stop) using plastic, oceans would be cleaner.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if': simple past en el segundo condicional.

exercises.question: Animals _____ (not / be) endangered if we protected their habitats.
exercises.explanation: Resultado hipotético negativo: wouldn't + infinitivo.

exercises.question: What _____ you _____ (do) if you were an environmental activist?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con segundo condicional: What would + sujeto + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If we would reduce emissions, the planet would recover.
exercises.answer: If we reduced emissions, the planet would recover.
exercises.explanation: La cláusula 'if' del segundo condicional NO usa 'would'. Solo simple past.

exercises.question: If there were less pollution, life will be better.
exercises.answer: If there were less pollution, life would be better.
exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional: cláusula resultado usa 'would', no 'will'.

exercises.question: We _____ reduce our carbon footprint immediately.
exercises.explanation: 'Must' para obligación fuerte o necesidad urgente.

exercises.question: Factories _____ release toxic waste into rivers.
exercises.explanation: 'Shouldn't' para indicar que algo es incorrecto o dañino.

exercises.question: Everyone _____ do their part to fight climate change.
exercises.explanation: 'Should' para obligación moral o recomendación.

exercises.question: Governments _____ invest more in renewable energy.
exercises.explanation: 'Ought to' = 'should': obligación moral. Lleva 'to'.

exercises.question: We _____ waste so much food — it contributes to emissions.
exercises.explanation: 'Mustn't' para prohibición fuerte. 'Shouldn't' también es aceptable.

exercises.question: Companies _____ (be) more responsible for their waste.
exercises.explanation: Obligación fuerte: must + infinitivo.

exercises.question: We _____ (not / cut) down any more forests.
exercises.explanation: Consejo/obligación negativa: shouldn't + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Children _____ (learn) about environmental issues at school.
exercises.explanation: Recomendación: should + infinitivo.

exercises.question: We must to protect the environment.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'must' NO va 'to'. Solo: must + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Factories should to stop polluting.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'should' NO va 'to'. Solo: should + infinitivo.

exercises.question: The journalist said the story _____ true.
exercises.explanation: Estilo indirecto: 'is' pasa a 'was'.

exercises.question: The editor told reporters they _____ verify their sources.
exercises.explanation: 'Must' en estilo indirecto se convierte en 'had to'.

exercises.question: She said she _____ the article by Monday.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' pasa a 'would' en el estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: He asked the presenter what _____ going to report next.
exercises.explanation: En preguntas indirectas el orden es sujeto + verbo (no se invierte).

exercises.question: The report stated that social media _____ a huge impact on young people.
exercises.explanation: Estilo indirecto: 'has' (presente) pasa a 'had' (pasado).

exercises.question: Direct: 'I found the fake news.' → She said she _____ the fake news.
exercises.explanation: Simple past pasa a past perfect en estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: Direct: 'Stop spreading misinformation!' → He told them _____ misinformation.
exercises.explanation: Reported command: told + objeto + to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: The editor asked _____ the article was ready.
exercises.explanation: Reported question con yes/no: asked + if/whether + sujeto + verbo.

exercises.question: The journalist said 'I was there yesterday'.
exercises.answer: The journalist said she had been there the day before.
exercises.explanation: Estilo indirecto: 'was' → 'had been'; 'yesterday' → 'the day before'.

exercises.question: She told that the news was fake.
exercises.answer: She said that the news was fake.
exercises.explanation: 'Say' no necesita objeto de persona (she said that). 'Tell' sí: she told us that.

exercises.question: The news _____ at 9 pm every evening.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente: is/are + past participle. 'News' es singular en inglés.

exercises.question: The article _____ by millions of people last week.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was/were + past participle.

exercises.question: The video _____ on several social media platforms.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was + past participle.

exercises.question: The documentary _____ next month.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de futuro: will + be + past participle.

exercises.question: The fake news story _____ quickly by fact-checkers.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was + past participle.

exercises.question: The interview _____ (film) in the studio.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva simple past: was + past participle.

exercises.question: Millions of photos _____ (upload) every day.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva presente plural: are + past participle.

exercises.question: The story _____ (not / verify) before publication.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva negativa: was not + past participle.

exercises.question: The podcast was record by a professional.
exercises.answer: The podcast was recorded by a professional.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva: was + past participle (recorded, no record).

exercises.question: The article were written yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Sujeto singular (the article) usa 'was', no 'were'.

exercises.question: The journalist _____ broke the story won an award.
exercises.explanation: 'Who' para personas en cláusulas relativas.

exercises.question: The platform _____ banned the account is the largest social network.
exercises.explanation: 'Which' para cosas/organizaciones.

exercises.question: The algorithm _____ content is shown to users is called a filter bubble.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' para indicar posesión.

exercises.question: That's the podcast _____ changed my opinion on the topic.
exercises.explanation: 'That' puede usarse para cosas (informal). 'Which' también sería correcto.

exercises.question: The editor _____ reviews the articles is very strict.
exercises.explanation: 'Who' para personas.

exercises.question: The social media post _____ went viral was a fake.
exercises.explanation: 'That' o 'which' para cosas.

exercises.question: The reporter _____ interview I watched was very professional.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' para posesión.

exercises.question: The app _____ users shared the most content was banned.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose users' indica posesión.

exercises.question: The website which it has fake news should be closed.
exercises.answer: The website which has fake news should be closed.
exercises.explanation: 'Which' ya funciona como sujeto, no se necesita 'it'.

exercises.question: The journalist what wrote the article has won many awards.
exercises.answer: The journalist who wrote the article has won many awards.
exercises.explanation: 'What' no se usa en cláusulas relativas. Para personas: 'who'.

exercises.question: I _____ social media for hours and I can't stop.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous: have/has been + -ing. Acción que empezó antes y continúa.

exercises.question: She _____ podcasts all morning.
exercises.explanation: Tercera persona: has been + -ing.

exercises.question: How long _____ you been watching that series?
exercises.explanation: 'How long + have/has + sujeto + been + -ing' para duración de una actividad.

exercises.question: They _____ their documentary for three years.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous para acción en progreso desde el pasado hasta ahora.

exercises.question: He _____ a lot lately — his eyes are red.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous enfatiza la duración/continuidad de la actividad.

exercises.question: We _____ (watch) the news all evening.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous: have been + -ing.

exercises.question: How long _____ she _____ (follow) this influencer?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta con present perfect continuous (tercera persona).

exercises.question: They _____ (post) fake news since last year.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous con 'since' (punto en el tiempo).

exercises.question: I have been watch TV for two hours.
exercises.answer: I have been watching TV for two hours.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous: have been + gerundio (-ing), no infinitivo.

exercises.question: She has been read the article all morning.
exercises.answer: She has been reading the article all morning.
exercises.explanation: Present perfect continuous necesita el gerundio: has been reading.

exercises.question: I _____ study medicine. I already applied.
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' para planes ya decididos con anticipación.

exercises.question: The phone is ringing. I _____ answer it.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' para decisiones tomadas en el momento.

exercises.question: Look at those clouds. It _____ snow!
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' para predicciones basadas en evidencia visible.

exercises.question: I think electric cars _____ replace petrol cars eventually.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' para predicciones personales (opiniones sobre el futuro).

exercises.question: They _____ open a new office in Brazil next year. It's been planned for months.
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' para planes previamente decididos.

exercises.question: A: 'We need more coffee.' B: 'Don't worry, I _____ (make) some.'
exercises.explanation: 'Will' para ofrecimiento o decisión espontánea.

exercises.question: She _____ (move) to Portugal. She's already found a flat.
exercises.explanation: 'Going to' para plan decidido con evidencia.

exercises.question: I think he _____ (pass) the exam — he studied a lot.
exercises.explanation: 'Will' para predicción basada en una opinión.

exercises.question: I will to start a new course next month.
exercises.answer: I will start a new course next month.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'will' NO va 'to'. Solo: will + infinitivo.
