exercises.question: She going to travel abroad next year.
exercises.answer: She is going to travel abroad next year.
exercises.explanation: Se necesita el auxiliar 'is/am/are' antes de 'going to'.

exercises.question: If I pass my exams, I _____ go to university.
exercises.explanation: Primer condicional: resultado probable con 'will'.

exercises.question: I _____ start my own business if I save enough money.
exercises.explanation: Primer condicional: situación real y posible.

exercises.question: If she _____ the promotion, she'll be thrilled.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if' en primer condicional: presente simple (no 'will').

exercises.question: _____ you apply for the scholarship if you qualify?
exercises.explanation: Pregunta en primer condicional: Will + sujeto + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If we _____ this project on time, the client will be happy.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if': presente simple en el primer condicional.

exercises.question: If I _____ (get) the visa, I'll move abroad.
exercises.explanation: Cláusula 'if': presente simple en primer condicional.

exercises.question: She _____ (not / quit) her job unless she finds something better.
exercises.explanation: Resultado negativo: won't + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If they offer me the position, I _____ (accept) immediately.
exercises.explanation: Resultado del primer condicional: will + infinitivo.

exercises.question: If I will get a good grade, I'll celebrate.
exercises.answer: If I get a good grade, I'll celebrate.
exercises.explanation: En la cláusula 'if' del primer condicional NO se usa 'will'. Solo presente simple.

exercises.question: If she passes the exam, she would go to university.
exercises.answer: If she passes the exam, she will go to university.
exercises.explanation: Primer condicional (situación posible): resultado con 'will', no 'would'.

exercises.question: I won't apply _____ the salary is good.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' = 'if not'. I won't apply unless = I will only apply if the salary is good.

exercises.question: She'll retire early _____ she finds a new job she loves.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' introduce una condición negativa: solo si NO encuentra trabajo nuevo.

exercises.question: _____ you work hard, you won't achieve your goals.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' al inicio = 'If not': Unless you work hard = If you don't work hard.

exercises.question: You can borrow my car _____ you return it by 8.
exercises.explanation: 'As long as' = 'con la condición de que'. Introduce condición positiva.

exercises.question: I'll support your plan _____ it is realistic and affordable.
exercises.explanation: 'Provided that' = 'siempre que / con la condición de que'.

exercises.question: He won't change careers _____ something better comes along.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' = solo si no ocurre algo.

exercises.question: I'll stay in this job _____ the company offers me a raise.
exercises.explanation: 'As long as' introduce la condición para que algo ocurra.

exercises.question: _____ she gets more experience, she won't be promoted.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' al inicio de la oración = Si no...

exercises.question: Unless you will study, you won't pass.
exercises.answer: Unless you study, you won't pass.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'unless', igual que con 'if', se usa presente simple (no 'will').

exercises.question: I won't go unless if you come too.
exercises.answer: I won't go unless you come too.
exercises.explanation: No se combinan 'unless' e 'if' juntos. Son equivalentes, se usa uno u otro.

exercises.question: She decided _____ a new language.
exercises.explanation: 'Decide' se sigue de infinitivo con 'to': decide to + verb.

exercises.question: I enjoy _____ new things in my free time.
exercises.explanation: 'Enjoy' se sigue de gerundio (-ing): enjoy learning.

exercises.question: He avoided _____ difficult decisions.
exercises.explanation: 'Avoid' + gerundio: avoid making.

exercises.question: They plan _____ abroad after graduation.
exercises.explanation: 'Plan' + infinitivo con 'to': plan to work.

exercises.question: I'm thinking of _____ back to university.
exercises.explanation: Después de preposiciones (of, about, in, etc.) va el gerundio.

exercises.question: She hopes _____ (travel) the world before she turns 30.
exercises.explanation: 'Hope' + infinitivo con 'to': hope to travel.

exercises.question: He finished _____ (write) his novel last month.
exercises.explanation: 'Finish' + gerundio: finish writing.

exercises.question: I look forward to _____ (start) my new job.
exercises.explanation: 'Look forward to' + gerundio ('to' aquí es preposición, no infinitivo).

exercises.question: She wants going abroad for work.
exercises.answer: She wants to go abroad for work.
exercises.explanation: 'Want' + infinitivo con 'to': want to go (no want + gerundio).

exercises.question: I'm looking forward to see you.
exercises.answer: I'm looking forward to seeing you.
exercises.explanation: 'Look forward to' lleva gerundio: looking forward to seeing ('to' es preposición aquí).

exercises.question: If she _____ harder, she would have passed the exam.
exercises.explanation: Tercera condicional: if + past perfect en la cláusula if.

exercises.question: He wouldn't have missed the train if he _____ earlier.
exercises.explanation: Tercera condicional: la cláusula con 'if' usa past perfect.

exercises.question: If they _____ the map, they wouldn't have got lost.
exercises.explanation: Tercera condicional: if + had + participio pasado.

exercises.question: She _____ the job if she had applied.
exercises.explanation: Resultado en tercera condicional: would + have + participio pasado.

exercises.question: If I _____ (know) about the meeting, I would have come.
exercises.explanation: Tercera condicional: if + had known (past perfect de know).

exercises.question: They would have won the match if their best player _____ (play).
exercises.explanation: If + past perfect en tercera condicional.

exercises.question: If you _____ (tell) me, I would have helped you.
exercises.explanation: Tercera condicional: if + had told.

exercises.question: If she would have studied, she would have passed.
exercises.answer: If she had studied, she would have passed.
exercises.explanation: En la cláusula 'if' de la tercera condicional NO se usa 'would'; se usa past perfect: had studied.

exercises.question: He had passed the test if he had tried harder.
exercises.answer: He would have passed the test if he had tried harder.
exercises.explanation: El resultado de tercera condicional usa 'would have', no 'had'.

exercises.question: If we had left earlier, we would arrived on time.
exercises.answer: If we had left earlier, we would have arrived on time.
exercises.explanation: El resultado requiere 'would have arrived', no 'would arrived'.

exercises.question: I wish I _____ more time to finish the project.
exercises.explanation: Wish + past perfect expresa arrepentimiento por el pasado.

exercises.question: She wishes she _____ the opportunity when she was young.
exercises.explanation: Wish + past perfect para lamentar algo que no ocurrió.

exercises.question: They wish they _____ their house before the market crashed.
exercises.explanation: Wish + had + participio para arrepentimientos sobre el pasado.

exercises.question: He wishes he _____ (not spend) all his savings.
exercises.explanation: Wish + past perfect negativo para lamentar una acción pasada.

exercises.question: I wish I _____ (choose) a different career.
exercises.explanation: Wish + past perfect para expresar arrepentimiento sobre el pasado.

exercises.question: She wishes she would have studied medicine.
exercises.answer: She wishes she had studied medicine.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'wish' para arrepentimientos pasados se usa past perfect (had studied), no 'would have'.

exercises.question: If she had taken the job offer, she _____ in London now.
exercises.explanation: Condicional mixta: pasado (if + past perfect) → presente (would + infinitivo).

exercises.question: If I were more organised, I _____ remembered the appointment.
exercises.explanation: Condicional mixta: presente (if + past simple) → pasado (would have + pp).

exercises.question: If he hadn't dropped out of university, he _____ (be) a doctor now.
exercises.explanation: Condicional mixta: pasado irreal → consecuencia en el presente.

exercises.question: If I had been braver, I would be accepted that challenge.
exercises.answer: If I had been braver, I would have accepted that challenge.
exercises.explanation: Cuando el resultado también es pasado: would have accepted, no would be accepted.

exercises.question: My brother, _____ lives in Barcelona, is visiting next week.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining relative clause con sujeto persona usa 'who'. No se usa 'that'.

exercises.question: The report, _____ was published yesterday, received wide coverage.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining relative clause para cosas/ideas usa 'which', nunca 'that'.

exercises.question: The CEO, _____ decision was controversial, resigned last month.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' indica posesión en relative clauses (personas y cosas).

exercises.question: The meeting, _____ lasted three hours, was exhausting.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining relative clause para eventos usa 'which'.

exercises.question: Her latest novel, _____ I finished last night, was brilliant.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining clause para objetos: 'which' (no 'that').

exercises.question: My professor, _____ I respect enormously, retired this year.
exercises.explanation: Objeto persona en relative clause formal: 'whom'.

exercises.question: The bridge, _____ construction took five years, opened last month.
exercises.explanation: 'Whose' para posesión en non-defining relative clauses.

exercises.question: My sister, that works in finance, got promoted.
exercises.answer: My sister, who works in finance, got promoted.
exercises.explanation: En non-defining relative clauses NO se usa 'that'; con persona se usa 'who'.

exercises.question: The concert which I attended last night, was cancelled.
exercises.answer: The concert, which I attended last night, was cancelled.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses se separan por comas.

exercises.question: This theory, that has been proved many times, is still debated.
exercises.answer: This theory, which has been proved many times, is still debated.
exercises.explanation: Non-defining clause para cosas: 'which', nunca 'that'.

exercises.question: _____ I find most challenging is writing clearly under pressure.
exercises.explanation: Cleft sentence con 'What' enfatiza el sujeto: What I find… is…

exercises.question: It was Maria _____ solved the problem.
exercises.explanation: 'It was + noun + who/that' en cleft sentences. 'who' para personas.

exercises.question: _____ they wanted was more time, not more money.
exercises.explanation: What-cleft para enfatizar lo que alguien quería.

exercises.question: _____ surprised me most was her calm reaction.
exercises.explanation: What-cleft: What + clause + was + énfasis.

exercises.question: It was the lack of communication _____ caused the conflict.
exercises.explanation: It-cleft: It was + énfasis + that + resto de la oración.

exercises.question: It was her dedication which impressed everyone.
exercises.answer: It was her dedication that impressed everyone.
exercises.explanation: En it-cleft con cosas abstractas se usa 'that', no 'which'.

exercises.question: Never _____ such a complex case in my entire career.
exercises.explanation: Inversión con 'Never' al inicio: auxiliar + sujeto + verbo principal.

exercises.question: Not only _____ the deadline, but he also exceeded expectations.
exercises.explanation: 'Not only' al inicio provoca inversión: did + sujeto + verbo.

exercises.question: Rarely _____ such creativity in a first-year student.
exercises.explanation: Inversión con 'Rarely': auxiliar do + sujeto + verbo.

exercises.question: Hardly _____ (sit down) when the fire alarm went off.
exercises.explanation: Inversión con 'Hardly': Hardly + had + sujeto + participio.

exercises.question: Not until she read the report _____ (understand) the scale of the problem.
exercises.explanation: Inversión con 'Not until': did + sujeto + infinitivo.

exercises.question: Seldom I have encountered such honesty.
exercises.answer: Seldom have I encountered such honesty.
exercises.explanation: 'Seldom' al inicio requiere inversión: Seldom + have + I + participio.

exercises.question: No sooner had she arrived when the meeting started.
exercises.answer: No sooner had she arrived than the meeting started.
exercises.explanation: 'No sooner… than' (no 'when'): No sooner had she arrived than…

exercises.question: Little I did know about the difficulties ahead.
exercises.answer: Little did I know about the difficulties ahead.
exercises.explanation: 'Little' negativo al inicio provoca inversión: Little + did + I + know.

exercises.question: You _____ told me about the change in plans. I was completely unprepared.
exercises.explanation: 'Should have' expresa crítica o arrepentimiento por algo que no se hizo.

exercises.question: She _____ left already. Her coat isn't here.
exercises.explanation: 'Must have' expresa deducción lógica sobre el pasado.

exercises.question: I _____ won if I hadn't made that mistake at the end.
exercises.explanation: 'Could have' expresa posibilidad no realizada en el pasado.

exercises.question: They _____ been working all night. The report was finished by 6 a.m.
exercises.explanation: 'Must have been working' indica deducción lógica sobre actividad pasada.

exercises.question: He _____ (warn) us about the risks. We had no idea.
exercises.explanation: Should have + participio: crítica o arrepentimiento sobre el pasado.

exercises.question: They _____ (arrive) by now. I wonder what happened.
exercises.explanation: 'Should have arrived' = era de esperarse que ya hubieran llegado.

exercises.question: She _____ (be) exhausted after running the marathon.
exercises.explanation: 'Must have been' para deducción lógica sobre estado pasado.

exercises.question: You must to have told her the truth.
exercises.answer: You must have told her the truth.
exercises.explanation: Modal perfect: modal + have + participio. No se usa 'to' después de modales.

exercises.question: She should has finished by now.
exercises.answer: She should have finished by now.
exercises.explanation: Modal perfect: should + have (no 'has') + participio pasado.

exercises.question: They might have been forget the meeting.
exercises.answer: They might have forgotten the meeting.
exercises.explanation: Modal perfect: might have + participio pasado (forgotten, no 'forget').

exercises.question: The results _____ to be published next month.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva con verbo de reporte: are expected + to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: The report _____ carefully before being submitted.
exercises.explanation: Modal + be + participio pasado para pasiva con modal.

exercises.question: It _____ that the project will be delayed.
exercises.explanation: Construcción impersonal pasiva: It is believed that…

exercises.question: The suspect is said _____ (flee) the country.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de reporte: is said + to have + participio (acción anterior al verbo principal).

exercises.question: The new regulations _____ (implement) by January.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva en future perfect: will have been + participio.

exercises.question: The research is believed to completed successfully.
exercises.answer: The research is believed to have been completed successfully.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de reporte en tiempo pasado: to have been + participio.

exercises.question: The policy was effective. _____, it had some unintended consequences.
exercises.explanation: 'Nevertheless' introduce contraste o concesión: a pesar de todo.

exercises.question: The evidence is overwhelming. _____, some experts remain unconvinced.
exercises.explanation: 'Nonetheless' indica contraste con algo dicho antes: sin embargo.

exercises.question: She failed the first time. _____, she tried again and succeeded.
exercises.explanation: 'Nevertheless' indica persistencia a pesar de un obstáculo.

exercises.question: The costs are high. _____, the long-term benefits justify the investment.
exercises.explanation: Discourse marker de contraste entre costes y beneficios.

exercises.question: The new law was controversial. _____, it passed with a large majority.
exercises.explanation: 'Nonetheless' para concesión formal en escritura académica.

exercises.question: The results were poor, however the team celebrated anyway.
exercises.answer: The results were poor; however, the team celebrated anyway.
exercises.explanation: 'However' como conjunción conectora requiere punto y coma antes y coma después.

exercises.question: _____ the difficulties involved, the team completed the project on time.
exercises.explanation: 'Despite' + nombre/gerundio (no + cláusula). 'Although' y 'even though' van con cláusula.

exercises.question: _____ she worked very hard, she didn't get the promotion.
exercises.explanation: 'Although' + cláusula (sujeto + verbo) para introducir concesión.

exercises.question: _____ of the negative reviews, the film was a box office success.
exercises.explanation: 'In spite of' (no 'In spite') + nombre. Equivalente a 'despite'.

exercises.question: _____ being exhausted, she agreed to work the extra shift.
exercises.explanation: 'Despite' + gerundio para concesión sin cláusula completa.

exercises.question: _____ the high cost, the quality makes it a worthwhile investment.
exercises.explanation: 'Despite' + nombre/frase nominal para concesión.

exercises.question: He passed the exam _____ barely studying.
exercises.explanation: 'Despite' + gerundio para concesión informal.

exercises.question: _____ the company was struggling, the CEO remained optimistic.
exercises.explanation: 'Although' + sujeto + verbo para cláusula de concesión.

exercises.question: Despite she worked hard, the business failed.
exercises.answer: Despite working hard, the business failed.
exercises.explanation: 'Despite' NO va seguido de sujeto + verbo. Usa 'Despite + gerundio' o 'Although + cláusula'.

exercises.question: In spite the difficulties, they succeeded.
exercises.answer: In spite of the difficulties, they succeeded.
exercises.explanation: 'In spite of' siempre lleva 'of': In spite of + nombre.

exercises.question: Although being tired, she kept going.
exercises.answer: Despite being tired, she kept going.
exercises.explanation: 'Although' requiere cláusula completa. Con gerundio se usa 'despite'.

exercises.question: I'd rather you _____ me before making that decision.
exercises.explanation: 'Would rather + sujeto diferente + past simple' para preferencia presente/futura.

exercises.question: It's high time the government _____ action on this issue.
exercises.explanation: 'It's high time + past simple' indica que algo debería haber ocurrido ya.

exercises.question: I'd sooner _____ than admit I was wrong.
exercises.explanation: 'Would sooner + infinitivo sin to' para preferencia fuerte.

exercises.question: I'd rather you _____ (not tell) anyone about this yet.
exercises.explanation: 'Would rather + sujeto diferente + past simple negativo'.

exercises.question: It's about time we _____ (have) this conversation.
exercises.explanation: 'It's about time + past simple' para urgencia o tardanza.

exercises.question: It's high time you will make a decision.
exercises.answer: It's high time you made a decision.
exercises.explanation: 'It's high time' usa past simple (no futuro): It's high time you made...

exercises.question: I'd rather you don't share this information.
exercises.answer: I'd rather you didn't share this information.
exercises.explanation: 'Would rather + sujeto diferente' usa past simple: didn't share.

exercises.question: The _____ of the new policy caused widespread concern.
exercises.explanation: Nominalización: el verbo 'introduce' se convierte en nombre 'introduction'.

exercises.question: The _____ of the agreement took months of negotiation.
exercises.explanation: Nominalización formal: 'finalise' → 'finalisation'.

exercises.question: The _____ (develop) of new vaccines requires significant investment.
exercises.explanation: Nominalización: 'develop' → 'development'.

exercises.question: There has been a significant _____ (improve) in air quality.
exercises.explanation: Nominalización: 'improve' → 'improvement'.

exercises.question: The investigate of the incident is ongoing.
exercises.answer: The investigation of the incident is ongoing.
exercises.explanation: Nominalización correcta: 'investigate' → 'investigation'.

exercises.question: I am writing to _____ my dissatisfaction with the service provided.
exercises.explanation: 'Express dissatisfaction' es la colocación formal correcta.

exercises.question: We would be grateful if you could _____ at your earliest convenience.
exercises.explanation: 'Respond' es el verbo formal preferido; 'reply to' también es correcto pero no 'reply us'.

exercises.question: Please _____ that we cannot accept liability for losses incurred.
exercises.explanation: 'Please be advised that' es fórmula formal estándar para avisos.

exercises.question: We _____ (appreciate) your continued support in this matter.
exercises.explanation: Registro formal: 'would appreciate' es más cortés que 'appreciate'.

exercises.question: I would like to draw your _____ to the attached document.
exercises.explanation: 'Draw attention to' es la colocación formal correcta.

exercises.question: I'm writing to complain about the bad service.
exercises.answer: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the quality of service provided.
exercises.explanation: Registro formal evita contracciones y usa vocabulario preciso: 'express dissatisfaction' no 'complain about bad'.

exercises.question: We are sorry to inform you that we can't help.
exercises.answer: We regret to inform you that we are unable to assist.
exercises.explanation: Registro formal: 'regret to inform', 'unable to assist' (no 'can't help').

exercises.question: The new policy _____ to reduce unemployment by 5% within two years.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de reporte: is expected + to + infinitivo.

exercises.question: It _____ that significant reforms will be necessary.
exercises.explanation: Construcción impersonal pasiva: It is widely acknowledged that…

exercises.question: Several witnesses _____ to have seen the suspect near the building.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de reporte: are reported + to + have + participio.

exercises.question: The project _____ (complete) by the end of the year, according to the director.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de reporte en forma continua: is expected + to be + participio.

exercises.question: It _____ (allege) that the company misled investors.
exercises.explanation: Construcción impersonal pasiva: It is alleged that…

exercises.question: The suspect is reported to fled the country.
exercises.answer: The suspect is reported to have fled the country.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva de reporte en tiempo pasado: is reported + to have + participio.

exercises.question: It is believed by most scientists that the results are accurate.
exercises.answer: It is believed that the results are accurate.
exercises.explanation: En construcciones impersonales pasivas, el agente generalmente se omite si es obvio.

exercises.question: _____ is transparency that the public demands most from politicians.
exercises.explanation: It-cleft: 'It is + énfasis + that + cláusula'.

exercises.question: _____ I find most frustrating about bureaucracy is its inflexibility.
exercises.explanation: What-cleft: 'What + cláusula + is + énfasis'.

exercises.question: _____ concerns me most is the lack of long-term planning.
exercises.explanation: What-cleft para enfatizar el sujeto de la oración.

exercises.question: _____ was the failure to communicate that led to the crisis.
exercises.explanation: It-cleft: 'It was + causa + that + efecto'.

exercises.question: What concerns me most are the long-term consequences.
exercises.answer: What concerns me most is the long-term consequences.
exercises.explanation: La cláusula 'what' es gramaticalmente singular; usa 'is', no 'are'.

exercises.question: By the time you arrive, I _____ the report.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect: will + have + participio para acción completada antes de un momento futuro.

exercises.question: By 2050, scientists _____ a cure for several currently incurable diseases.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect con referencia temporal futura ('By 2050').

exercises.question: She _____ this project for three years by the time it's finished.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect continuous para duración hasta un punto futuro.

exercises.question: By the end of the decade, the city _____ (transform) completely.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect: will have + participio.

exercises.question: Don't call at 9 p.m. — I _____ (sleep) by then.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect para acción que habrá ocurrido antes de un momento futuro.

exercises.question: By the time they publish the findings, the landscape _____ (change) dramatically.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect para enfatizar la completitud de una acción futura.

exercises.question: By next year, she will complete her PhD.
exercises.answer: By next year, she will have completed her PhD.
exercises.explanation: 'By + tiempo futuro' requiere future perfect: will have completed.

exercises.question: They would have finished by the time we arrive.
exercises.answer: They will have finished by the time we arrive.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect usa 'will have', no 'would have' (eso es condicional).

exercises.question: She told me she _____ never seen anything like it in her career.
exercises.explanation: Reported speech: presente perfecto → past perfect en estilo indirecto.

exercises.question: He denied _____ the documents.
exercises.explanation: 'Deny + gerundio/having + participio' para negación en reported speech.

exercises.question: The minister claimed that the figures _____ misinterpreted.
exercises.explanation: Reported speech: presente perfecto pasivo → past perfect pasivo.

exercises.question: She admitted _____ (make) a mistake in the calculations.
exercises.explanation: 'Admit + having + participio' en reported speech.

exercises.question: He insisted that the decision _____ (not reverse).
exercises.explanation: Reported speech con pasiva: insisted that + would + be + participio.

exercises.question: She explained that she has been working on it for months.
exercises.answer: She explained that she had been working on it for months.
exercises.explanation: Reported speech: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: He told that the report would be delayed.
exercises.answer: He said that the report would be delayed.
exercises.explanation: 'Tell' requiere objeto (told me/us); sin objeto se usa 'said that'.

exercises.question: The data suggests that the correlation between the variables _____ statistically significant.
exercises.explanation: 'The correlation' es sujeto singular: is.

exercises.question: This phenomenon _____ be attributed to a combination of social and economic factors.
exercises.explanation: 'Can be attributed to' para relaciones causales en escritura académica.

exercises.question: The findings of this study _____ with those of earlier research.
exercises.explanation: 'Are consistent with' para comparar hallazgos de investigación.

exercises.question: It _____ (argue) that these results challenge the existing framework.
exercises.explanation: 'It can be argued that' es estructura académica para presentar argumentos.

exercises.question: The evidence _____ (suggest) a causal rather than correlational relationship.
exercises.explanation: 'The evidence suggests' (singular, presente simple) en escritura académica.

exercises.question: This study demonstrates that the previous assumptions were wrong.
exercises.answer: This study suggests that the previous assumptions may have been flawed.
exercises.explanation: Escritura académica usa lenguaje más hedged: 'suggests' (no 'demonstrates'), 'may have been flawed' (no 'were wrong').

exercises.question: We can clearly see that poverty causes crime.
exercises.answer: The data suggests a correlation between poverty and crime, though causation remains contested.
exercises.explanation: En escritura académica se evita 'we', se usa lenguaje matizado sobre causalidad.

exercises.question: The constitution requires that every candidate _____ born within the country's borders.
exercises.explanation: El subjuntivo formal usa la forma base del verbo: 'requires that + subject + base verb'.

exercises.question: It is imperative that Parliament _____ without delay on the proposed amendment.
exercises.explanation: Con 'It is imperative that', se usa el subjuntivo: forma base sin -s.

exercises.question: The electoral commission insisted that all ballots _____ counted in public.
exercises.explanation: Subjuntivo formal pasivo: 'insisted that + subject + be + past participle'.

exercises.question: It is essential that the judiciary _____ independent of all political interference.
exercises.explanation: Subjuntivo formal: 'It is essential that + subject + base verb'.

exercises.question: The law requires that every defendant has access to legal representation.
exercises.answer: The law requires that every defendant have access to legal representation.
exercises.explanation: El subjuntivo formal usa 'have', no 'has', después de 'requires that'.

exercises.question: It is essential that the committee considers all the evidence before delivering its verdict.
exercises.answer: It is essential that the committee consider all the evidence before delivering its verdict.
exercises.explanation: Con 'It is essential that', el subjuntivo exige la forma base: 'consider', no 'considers'.

exercises.question: The treaty stipulates that each signatory _____ its ratification documents within sixty days.
exercises.explanation: Subjuntivo formal: 'stipulates that + subject + base verb'.

exercises.question: The protocol demands that the ambassador _____ his credentials within one week.
exercises.explanation: Subjuntivo formal: 'demands that + subject + base verb' sin -s.

exercises.question: _____ the prime minister resigned earlier, the constitutional crisis could have been avoided.
exercises.explanation: 'Had + subject + past participle' expresa una condición irreal pasada (inversión formal de 3ª condicional).

exercises.question: _____ it not for the constitutional safeguards, the amendment would have passed unchallenged.
exercises.explanation: 'Were it not for' = inversión formal para condiciones hipotéticas presentes.

exercises.question: _____ you require any clarification regarding the electoral procedure, please contact the commission.
exercises.explanation: 'Should you + base verb' es la inversión formal de 'If you should need'.

exercises.question: _____ the government known about the intelligence report, it would have acted immediately.
exercises.explanation: 'Had + subject + pp' = inversión de 3ª condicional: condición irreal pasada.

exercises.question: _____ it necessary, the president could invoke emergency constitutional powers.
exercises.explanation: 'Were it + adjective' = inversión hipotética formal equivalente a 'If it were necessary'.

exercises.question: If it not for the opposition's intervention, the vote would have passed unanimously.
exercises.answer: Were it not for the opposition's intervention, the vote would have passed unanimously.
exercises.explanation: La forma correcta de la inversión hipotética es 'Were it not for', no 'If it not for'.

exercises.question: Had I have known about the plan, I would have alerted the authorities immediately.
exercises.answer: Had I known about the plan, I would have alerted the authorities immediately.
exercises.explanation: Con la inversión de 3ª condicional se usa 'Had + subject + pp' sin 'have' adicional.

exercises.question: _____ the legislation been implemented ten years earlier, the situation today would be different.
exercises.explanation: 'Had + subject + pp': inversión de 3ª condicional para condición irreal pasada.

exercises.question: It is high time the electorate _____ politicians to a higher standard of accountability.
exercises.explanation: 'It is high time + past simple' expresa que algo debería haberse hecho ya.

exercises.question: If only the legislation _____ enacted before the crisis reached its peak.
exercises.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' expresa arrepentimiento sobre el pasado.

exercises.question: I would rather the government _____ the classified documents to the public sooner.
exercises.explanation: 'Would rather + past perfect' expresa preferencia sobre una acción pasada.

exercises.question: It is time that citizens demand greater transparency from their elected representatives.
exercises.answer: It is time that citizens demanded greater transparency from their elected representatives.
exercises.explanation: 'It is time that + past simple': la forma pasada expresa urgencia o crítica.

exercises.question: If only the opposition _____ united before the vote; the outcome might have been different.
exercises.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' expresa lamentación sobre una situación pasada irreal.

exercises.question: I would rather politicians _____ honest about the fiscal challenges from the very beginning.
exercises.explanation: 'Would rather + past perfect' expresa preferencia retrospectiva sobre una acción pasada.

exercises.question: She stopped _____ the ontological argument when she found a fundamental logical flaw.
exercises.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' = dejar de hacer algo; 'stop to + infinitivo' = detenerse para hacer algo.

exercises.question: Remember _____ cite your primary sources whenever you present a philosophical claim.
exercises.explanation: 'Remember + to-infinitivo' = recordar hacer algo aún pendiente.

exercises.question: She remembered _____ this exact argument in her first philosophy seminar many years ago.
exercises.explanation: 'Remember + gerund' = recordar una experiencia pasada ya ocurrida.

exercises.question: He tried _____ the utilitarian framework, but the results were counterintuitive.
exercises.explanation: 'Try + gerund' = experimentar con algo como prueba.

exercises.question: She tried _____ reconcile Kant's deontology with consequentialist outcomes but failed.
exercises.explanation: 'Try + to-infinitivo' = esforzarse para lograr algo.

exercises.question: He regretted _____ (publish) his early conclusions before completing the full study.
exercises.explanation: 'Regret + having + pp' expresa arrepentimiento por algo ya hecho.

exercises.question: She went on _____ (develop) a more nuanced ethical framework in her later work.
exercises.explanation: 'Go on + to-infinitivo' = continuar con algo diferente a lo anterior.

exercises.question: Working as a moral philosopher means _____ that many fundamental questions resist definitive answers.
exercises.explanation: 'Mean + gerund' = implicar / involucrar algo.

exercises.question: He forgot bringing his argument notes and could not defend his thesis properly.
exercises.answer: He forgot to bring his argument notes and could not defend his thesis properly.
exercises.explanation: 'Forget + to-infinitivo' = olvidarse de hacer algo (la acción no ocurrió).

exercises.question: She stopped to worry about determinism after reading the compatibilist literature.
exercises.answer: She stopped worrying about determinism after reading the compatibilist literature.
exercises.explanation: 'Stopped to worry' = se detuvo para preocuparse; 'stopped worrying' = ya no se preocupaba. El segundo tiene sentido aquí.

exercises.question: He meant _____ (challenge) the established view, not simply restate it in different terms.
exercises.explanation: 'Mean + to-infinitivo' = tener la intención de hacer algo.

exercises.question: I regret _____ you that your paper does not meet the academic standards for publication.
exercises.explanation: 'Regret + to-infinitivo' = lamentarse de decir algo ahora (fórmula formal para malas noticias).

exercises.question: The philosopher appears _____ this concept from the Kantian tradition.
exercises.explanation: El perfect infinitivo expresa que la acción ocurrió antes del tiempo del verbo principal.

exercises.question: She seems _____ (misunderstand) the central premise based on her counterargument.
exercises.explanation: 'Seem + to have + pp' describe una acción previa al momento presente.

exercises.question: He claims _____ discovered a logical contradiction that undermines the entire argument.
exercises.explanation: 'Claim + to have + pp' = alegar haber realizado algo en el pasado.

exercises.question: The manuscript is believed _____ (write) anonymously in the seventeenth century.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva con infinitivo perfecto: 'is believed + to have been + pp'.

exercises.question: The theory turned out _____ far more influential than its critics had initially acknowledged.
exercises.explanation: 'Turned out + to have been' indica algo que resultó ser verdad retrospectivamente.

exercises.question: She claims to discover a fundamental flaw in Aristotle's original logic.
exercises.answer: She claims to have discovered a fundamental flaw in Aristotle's original logic.
exercises.explanation: Cuando la acción ya ocurrió, se usa 'claim + to have + pp', no 'claim + to + base verb'.

exercises.question: He appears _____ (arrive) at this conclusion independently, without knowledge of prior research.
exercises.explanation: 'Appear + to have + pp' = parecer haber hecho algo antes del momento presente.

exercises.question: The ancient text is said _____ written by a student of Socrates.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva con infinitivo perfecto: 'is said + to have been + pp'.

exercises.question: She seems to understand the paradox when she first read it as a student.
exercises.answer: She seems to have understood the paradox when she first read it as a student.
exercises.explanation: Cuando la comprensión ocurrió en el pasado, se usa 'seem + to have + pp'.

exercises.question: The concept is thought _____ (originate) in ancient Greek philosophy before being codified by Aristotle.
exercises.explanation: 'Is thought + to have + pp' = se cree que ocurrió antes del tiempo de referencia.

exercises.question: The first study found a significant effect, and _____.
exercises.explanation: Ellipsis formal: 'so + auxiliary + subject' para evitar repetir el verbo y complemento.

exercises.question: Neither _____ the control group show a statistically significant result.
exercises.explanation: Ellipsis negativa: 'Neither + auxiliary + subject' = tampoco lo hizo.

exercises.question: The data supports the hypothesis. The replications _____.
exercises.explanation: 'Do so' sustituye a 'support the hypothesis' para evitar repetición.

exercises.question: The first trial produced unreliable results; the second _____ as well.
exercises.explanation: Ellipsis con 'did' para sustituir el verbo completo: 'produced unreliable results'.

exercises.question: She revised the methodology. So her supervisor has.
exercises.answer: She revised the methodology. So did her supervisor.
exercises.explanation: La forma correcta de la ellipsis afirmativa es 'So + auxiliary + subject' en el mismo tiempo verbal.

exercises.question: Team A completed the analysis and Team B _____ too.
exercises.explanation: 'Did so' = ellipsis formal que sustituye 'completed the analysis'.

exercises.question: The study was peer-reviewed. The follow-up study _____ too.
exercises.explanation: Ellipsis con auxiliar: 'was' sustituye 'was peer-reviewed'.

exercises.question: Two theories were proposed: the cognitive and the social. The _____ has more empirical support.
exercises.explanation: 'The latter' se refiere al segundo de dos elementos mencionados previamente.

exercises.question: Between behavioural and cognitive approaches, the _____ focuses on internal mental processes.
exercises.explanation: 'The latter' = el segundo de los dos mencionados (cognitive).

exercises.question: The above conclusions are tentative. So the preliminary findings are.
exercises.answer: The above conclusions are tentative. So are the preliminary findings.
exercises.explanation: La inversión correcta con 'so' es 'So + auxiliary + subject'.

exercises.question: The quantitative and qualitative methodologies were both used. The _____ yielded richer contextual data.
exercises.explanation: 'The former' se refiere al primer elemento mencionado (quantitative).

exercises.question: The findings of the meta-analysis contradict _____ of the individual studies.
exercises.explanation: 'Those' sustituye a 'the findings' del segundo conjunto, evitando repetición.

exercises.question: If the null hypothesis is rejected, the alternative _____.
exercises.explanation: Substitución con el auxiliar apropiado para evitar repetición del verbo completo.

exercises.question: The original experiment was replicated three times. Each replication _____ the same methodology.
exercises.explanation: 'Do so' sustituye el verbo principal; permite añadir información adicional.

exercises.question: _____ the limitations of the study, the findings provide significant insight into the phenomenon.
exercises.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' = a pesar de (formal, académico); nunca 'despite of'.

exercises.question: The policy is ineffective _____ as it fails to address the root causes of the problem.
exercises.explanation: 'Insofar as' = en la medida en que (marcador académico formal).

exercises.question: _____ the evidence presented, the committee remains unconvinced of the causal relationship.
exercises.explanation: 'In light of' = teniendo en cuenta / a la luz de.

exercises.question: The study is flawed inasmuch it relies on a non-representative sample.
exercises.answer: The study is flawed inasmuch as it relies on a non-representative sample.
exercises.explanation: 'Inasmuch as' lleva 'as'; sin él la frase es agramatical.

exercises.question: _____ the previous research, this study adopts a longitudinal rather than cross-sectional design.
exercises.explanation: 'Unlike' = a diferencia de (preposición que introduce contraste formal).

exercises.question: _____ respect to the methodology, the researchers chose a mixed-methods approach.
exercises.explanation: 'With respect to' = con respecto a / en cuanto a (marcador de tema académico).

exercises.question: Notwithstanding to the challenges, the research team maintained rigorous standards throughout.
exercises.answer: Notwithstanding the challenges, the research team maintained rigorous standards throughout.
exercises.explanation: 'Notwithstanding' es preposición; no va seguida de 'to'.

exercises.question: The results are valid _____ the conditions specified in the original protocol were maintained.
exercises.explanation: 'Provided that' = siempre y cuando / con la condición de que (formal).

exercises.question: _____ until the leaked documents were published that the full extent of the cover-up became known.
exercises.explanation: La cleft negativa temporal usa 'It was not until + evento + that + resultado'.

exercises.question: It was the investigative journalist, not the government, _____ first revealed the scandal.
exercises.explanation: La it-cleft usa 'who' para personas y 'that' para cosas.

exercises.question: What _____ most about the coverage was the absence of alternative perspectives.
exercises.explanation: 'What + had + pp' en una what-cleft para enfatizar algo en el pasado.

exercises.question: _____ the editor did was remove the critical paragraphs without the journalist's knowledge.
exercises.explanation: La what-cleft comienza con 'What + subject + verb + was'.

exercises.question: It was not until that the story broke that the public became aware of the manipulation.
exercises.answer: It was not until the story broke that the public became aware of the manipulation.
exercises.explanation: La estructura correcta es 'not until + clause' sin el 'that' adicional entre 'until' y la cláusula.

exercises.question: What had analysts warned about for years _____ the lack of regulatory oversight in social media.
exercises.explanation: En la what-cleft, el verbo copulativo concuerda con el complemento singular.

exercises.question: It was the algorithm, not the editorial team, _____ determined what millions of users read.
exercises.explanation: En la it-cleft para conceptos/cosas, se usa 'that'.

exercises.question: What _____ audiences about deepfake technology is the growing difficulty of detecting fabricated content.
exercises.explanation: La what-cleft con sujeto singular requiere verbo en tercera persona singular.

exercises.question: What the whistleblower done was expose a systematic pattern of editorial suppression.
exercises.answer: What the whistleblower did was expose a systematic pattern of editorial suppression.
exercises.explanation: La what-cleft usa el auxiliar correcto: 'what + subject + did + was'.

exercises.question: It was _____ the misinformation spread so rapidly that the platform's recommendation algorithm amplified it.
exercises.explanation: La it-cleft puede usar 'because' para enfatizar la razón de algo.

exercises.question: Not only _____ social media platforms failed to remove the content, but they actively amplified it.
exercises.explanation: 'Not only + have + subject + pp': inversión con present perfect.

exercises.question: Scarcely _____ the report been published when journalists began raising questions about its methodology.
exercises.explanation: 'Scarcely + had + subject + pp + when' para dos eventos pasados consecutivos.

exercises.question: Only when the evidence had been independently verified _____ the editor agree to publish the story.
exercises.explanation: 'Only when + clause + did + subject + base verb': inversión después de adverbio restrictivo.

exercises.question: Not since the Watergate scandal _____ the press faced such intense government pressure.
exercises.explanation: 'Not since + time + had + subject + pp' en pasado perfecto.

exercises.question: Only after the whistleblower came forward did the full truth came to light.
exercises.answer: Only after the whistleblower came forward did the full truth come to light.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'did' se usa el infinitivo sin inflexión: 'come to light', no 'came to light'.

exercises.question: No sooner _____ the retraction been published than the journalist filed a defamation lawsuit.
exercises.explanation: 'No sooner + had + subject + pp + than' expresa dos eventos pasados consecutivos.

exercises.question: Not until the story broke _____ the public become aware of the scale of the surveillance programme.
exercises.explanation: 'Not until + clause + did + subject + base verb': inversión con adverbio negativo.

exercises.question: Rarely _____ a single story have such an immediate and lasting impact on public policy.
exercises.explanation: 'Rarely + does + subject + base verb': inversión con adverbio de frecuencia negativo.

exercises.question: Only by investing in media literacy _____ society become more resistant to disinformation campaigns.
exercises.explanation: 'Only by + gerund + can/will + subject + base verb': inversión modal.

exercises.question: Not only the newspaper published the story, but it also ran an editorial calling for reform.
exercises.answer: Not only did the newspaper publish the story, but it also ran an editorial calling for reform.
exercises.explanation: 'Not only' al inicio de oración requiere inversión: 'Not only + did + subject + base verb'.

exercises.question: Never before _____ the public had access to so many sources of information simultaneously.
exercises.explanation: 'Never before + has + subject + pp': inversión con present perfect.

exercises.question: Scarcely had the interview ended when did the presenter receive a legal threat.
exercises.answer: Scarcely had the interview ended when the presenter received a legal threat.
exercises.explanation: Después de 'when' en esta estructura no hay inversión.

exercises.question: The government _____ independent experts _____ the environmental impact study.
exercises.explanation: 'Have + object + past participle' = causative pasivo (alguien realizó la acción por encargo).

exercises.question: The company _____ its carbon footprint _____ (audit) by a third party before the report was published.
exercises.explanation: 'Have + object + pp' expresa que otro realizó la acción por mandato.

exercises.question: She _____ the environmental lawyer _____ her case before submitting the climate litigation.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + to-infinitivo' = pedir o lograr que alguien haga algo.

exercises.question: The municipality _____ the river _____ (clean) after evidence of industrial contamination was found.
exercises.explanation: 'Had + object + pp': la autoridad municipal mandó que limpiaran el río.

exercises.question: The city got the new green infrastructure to install by a local contractor.
exercises.answer: The city got the new green infrastructure installed by a local contractor.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + pp' para el causative pasivo; 'to install' no es correcto en esta estructura.

exercises.question: The charity _____ native trees _____ across the degraded hillside to restore biodiversity.
exercises.explanation: 'Had + object + pp': la organización hizo que otros plantaran los árboles.

exercises.question: Environmental lawyers are advising communities to _____ the health impacts _____ (study) independently.
exercises.explanation: 'Have + object + pp' = encargar que se estudien los impactos de forma independiente.

exercises.question: The activist got the report to translate into twelve languages for wider distribution.
exercises.answer: The activist got the report translated into twelve languages for wider distribution.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + pp' para causative pasivo; no 'to translate' sino 'translated'.

exercises.question: Local authorities should _____ air quality _____ (monitor) continuously in areas near industrial sites.
exercises.explanation: 'Have + object + pp' expresa que la autoridad encarga el monitoreo a otros.

exercises.question: The policy _____ businesses _____ their full carbon accounting within two years.
exercises.explanation: 'Get + object + to-infinitivo' = conseguir / lograr que alguien haga algo.

exercises.question: It _____ that the tipping point for irreversible Arctic ice loss may already have been reached.
exercises.explanation: 'It has emerged that' = ha surgido / salido a la luz que (pasiva impersonal).

exercises.question: It _____ (come to light) that several corporations had been falsifying their emissions data.
exercises.explanation: 'It has come to light that' = se ha descubierto / revelado que.

exercises.question: It is widely _____ that the 2050 net zero targets will require unprecedented international cooperation.
exercises.explanation: 'It is widely acknowledged that' = se reconoce ampliamente que.

exercises.question: It _____ (report) that methane levels in the permafrost region have exceeded all previous projections.
exercises.explanation: Pasiva impersonal en present perfect: 'it has been reported that'.

exercises.question: It emerges that the cap-and-trade scheme had been poorly designed from the outset.
exercises.answer: It has emerged that the cap-and-trade scheme had been poorly designed from the outset.
exercises.explanation: El presente perfecto 'has emerged' es más natural para noticias recientes.

exercises.question: It has been _____ that the government was aware of the pollution levels years before taking action.
exercises.explanation: 'It has been established that' = se ha determinado / comprobado que.

exercises.question: It _____ (understand) that the new policy will exempt small businesses from the carbon tax requirements.
exercises.explanation: 'It is understood that' = se da por entendido / se entiende que.

exercises.question: It was transpired that the environmental agency had suppressed its own research findings.
exercises.answer: It transpired that the environmental agency had suppressed its own research findings.
exercises.explanation: 'Transpire' en este sentido no usa la forma pasiva; 'It transpired that' es activo.

exercises.question: It has long been _____ that biodiversity loss poses as serious a threat as climate change itself.
exercises.explanation: 'It has long been argued that' = se ha argumentado durante mucho tiempo que.

exercises.question: It was understood the carbon offset scheme would be reviewed after the first compliance period.
exercises.answer: It was understood that the carbon offset scheme would be reviewed after the first compliance period.
exercises.explanation: La pasiva impersonal requiere 'that' antes de la cláusula subordinada.

exercises.question: It _____ (come to light) that several nations had systematically overstated their renewable energy contributions.
exercises.explanation: 'It came to light that' = se reveló / se descubrió que (en pasado).

exercises.question: It would _____ that the deforestation rate had accelerated significantly following the change of government.
exercises.explanation: 'It would appear that' = al parecer / parecería que (con matiz de incertidumbre).

exercises.question: _____ the peace talks succeed, a framework for a permanent ceasefire will be established.
exercises.explanation: 'Assuming + clause': condicional que asume que algo es posible o probable.

exercises.question: The sanctions will be lifted _____ the government demonstrates verifiable compliance with the treaty.
exercises.explanation: 'Provided that' = siempre y cuando / con la condición de que.

exercises.question: The agreement will hold _____ all signatories honour their obligations under international law.
exercises.explanation: 'As long as' = siempre y cuando / mientras que.

exercises.question: _____ negotiations fail, the international community may resort to harsher economic measures.
exercises.explanation: 'Should + subject + base verb' = inversión formal de condicional de baja probabilidad.

exercises.question: The aid will be released _____ the humanitarian corridors are kept open and accessible.
exercises.explanation: 'On condition that' = con la condición de que.

exercises.question: Access to trade benefits will remain suspended _____ the human rights situation improves.
exercises.explanation: 'Unless' = a menos que / excepto si.

exercises.question: Supposing if the agreement collapses, the region could return to armed conflict.
exercises.answer: Supposing the agreement collapses, the region could return to armed conflict.
exercises.explanation: 'Supposing' ya funciona como condicional; no necesita 'if' adicional.

exercises.question: _____ the ceasefire holds, a joint peacekeeping force will be deployed within thirty days.
exercises.explanation: 'Provided + clause' (sin 'that') = siempre y cuando.

exercises.question: _____ that all parties maintain a genuine commitment to dialogue, a lasting settlement is achievable.
exercises.explanation: 'Given that' = dado que / suponiendo que.

exercises.question: On condition of that the sanctions are removed, the government has agreed to allow UN inspectors.
exercises.answer: On condition that the sanctions are removed, the government has agreed to allow UN inspectors.
exercises.explanation: 'On condition that': no se añade 'of' a esta expresión.

exercises.question: The extradition will proceed _____ the courts in both jurisdictions approve the transfer.
exercises.explanation: 'So long as' = siempre y cuando (equivalente a 'as long as').

exercises.question: _____ we appreciate the diplomatic efforts, the lack of enforcement mechanisms remains a serious concern.
exercises.explanation: 'Much as + clause' = aunque / si bien (concesión formal sin inversión).

exercises.question: _____ significant the progress in multilateral negotiations may be, the core disputes remain unresolved.
exercises.explanation: 'However + adjective + subject + may be': concesión formal con inversión modal.

exercises.question: _____ approach is taken by the international community, the root causes of the conflict must be addressed.
exercises.explanation: 'Whichever + noun + verb': concesión de opción (sea cual sea el enfoque).

exercises.question: _____ the short-term diplomatic costs, the long-term benefits of the agreement outweigh them.
exercises.explanation: 'Whatever + noun phrase' al inicio = sea cual sea / independientemente de.

exercises.question: However the situation may be difficult, both sides must remain committed to the negotiation process.
exercises.answer: However difficult the situation may be, both sides must remain committed to the negotiation process.
exercises.explanation: Con 'However', el adjetivo sigue inmediatamente: 'However + adj + subject + verb'.

exercises.question: _____ as they may be, diplomatic protocols must not prevent meaningful humanitarian intervention.
exercises.explanation: 'Adj + though + subject + may be' = por muy + adjetivo que sea (concesión formal).

exercises.question: _____ the geopolitical situation worsens, the international community has been slow to act decisively.
exercises.explanation: 'Much as + clause' concede la veracidad de la subordinada como concesión.

exercises.question: _____ the economic cost of sanctions, they remain one of the few non-military tools available.
exercises.explanation: 'Notwithstanding + noun phrase' = a pesar de (concesión formal).

exercises.question: _____ outcome the peace talks produce, compliance mechanisms must be in place from the outset.
exercises.explanation: 'Whatever + noun + clause' = sea cual sea el resultado.

exercises.question: Much as that the negotiations have been difficult, both parties have made substantial concessions.
exercises.answer: Much as the negotiations have been difficult, both parties have made substantial concessions.
exercises.explanation: 'Much as' no va seguido de 'that': 'Much as + clause' directamente.

exercises.question: However _____ the geopolitical challenges, the principles of international law must be upheld.
exercises.explanation: 'However + adj + subject + may be': estructura de concesión formal con modal.

exercises.question: A speaker who opens by listing their professional credentials and track record is primarily appealing to _____.
exercises.explanation: 'Ethos' = apelación a la credibilidad y autoridad del hablante.

exercises.question: Using statistics, data, and cause-effect arguments to make a case is primarily an appeal to _____.
exercises.explanation: 'Logos' = apelación a la razón mediante argumentos lógicos y evidencia.

exercises.question: A political speech that opens with a moving personal story of a family in poverty is designed primarily to appeal to _____.
exercises.explanation: 'Pathos' = apelación emocional. Las historias personales conmovedoras generan empatía.

exercises.question: In 'We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields', the repeated phrase is an example of _____.
exercises.explanation: La anáfora repite palabras al INICIO de cláusulas sucesivas.

exercises.question: 'Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country' inverts the structure. This is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El quiasmo invierte el orden de los elementos en frases paralelas: A-B / B-A.

exercises.question: 'You say we should cut the defence budget, but clearly you want the country defenceless.' This misrepresents the original position. It is a _____.
exercises.explanation: El hombre de paja distorsiona la posición del oponente para refutarla más fácilmente.

exercises.question: 'Either we implement these austerity measures or the economy will collapse.' Presenting only two options when others exist is a _____.
exercises.explanation: La falsa dicotomía presenta solo dos opciones cuando existen más alternativas.

exercises.question: Kennedy used _____ by repeating 'Let both sides...' at the beginning of successive clauses to create rhythmic emphasis.
exercises.explanation: La anáfora es la repetición de palabras o frases al inicio de unidades sintácticas consecutivas.

exercises.question: Referring to the same policy as 'tax relief' versus 'a tax cut for the wealthy' demonstrates how _____ shapes public perception of identical information.
exercises.explanation: El encuadre (framing) influye en la interpretación mediante la elección de palabras.

exercises.question: In academic writing, 'it would seem that' is an example of _____ language, which avoids stating a claim too absolutely.
exercises.explanation: El lenguaje de cobertura (hedging) atenúa las afirmaciones para no comprometerse más de lo que la evidencia permite.

exercises.question: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times' places opposing ideas in parallel structure. This is called _____.
exercises.explanation: La antítesis yuxtapone ideas opuestas en estructuras paralelas para crear contraste.

exercises.question: The question 'When did you stop lying to your colleagues?' contains a _____ — it assumes the person was lying.
exercises.explanation: Una presuposición es un supuesto embebido en una pregunta que el hablante da por sentado.

exercises.question: Acknowledging merit in an opposing view before countering it is called making a _____, typically introduced by 'admittedly' or 'while it is true that'.
exercises.explanation: La concesión retórica reconoce la validez parcial del argumento opuesto antes de refutarlo.

exercises.question: Saying 'The Holocaust was not exactly a minor administrative issue' uses deliberate _____ for rhetorical impact.
exercises.explanation: La subestimación expresa algo de forma menos intensa de lo que realmente es para enfatizar con ironía.

exercises.question: The speaker used pathos by presenting a detailed statistical analysis of economic data.
exercises.answer: The speaker used logos by presenting a detailed statistical analysis of economic data.
exercises.explanation: Los datos estadísticos y el análisis económico apelan a la razón (logos), no a la emoción (pathos).

exercises.question: His argument was an example of a straw dog — he distorted his opponent's position.
exercises.answer: His argument was an example of a straw man — he distorted his opponent's position.
exercises.explanation: La falacia se llama 'straw man' (hombre de paja), no 'straw dog'.

exercises.question: She ended each paragraph with the same phrase to create emphasis — this is an example of anaphora.
exercises.answer: She ended each paragraph with the same phrase to create emphasis — this is an example of epistrophe.
exercises.explanation: La epístrofe repite palabras al FINAL de cláusulas. La anáfora las repite al INICIO.

exercises.question: The CEO's speech was full of pathos because it quoted extensively from the quarterly earnings report.
exercises.answer: The CEO's speech was full of logos because it quoted extensively from the quarterly earnings report.
exercises.explanation: Citar datos de un informe financiero apela a la razón (logos), no a la emoción (pathos).

exercises.question: The phrase 'Live to work or work to live' is an example of antithesis.
exercises.answer: The phrase 'Live to work or work to live' is an example of chiasmus.
exercises.explanation: Invierte los elementos en orden A-B / B-A, lo que define el quiasmo, no la mera antítesis.

exercises.question: A question asked not to receive an answer but to create emphasis or make a point is called a _____ question.
exercises.explanation: Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta; su propósito es enfatizar o persuadir.

exercises.question: Describing protesters as 'freedom fighters' versus 'terrorists' for the same group exemplifies the power of _____ language.
exercises.explanation: El lenguaje cargado usa palabras con fuertes connotaciones para influir la percepción.

exercises.question: Which of these questions contains a hidden presupposition that assumes the listener has stopped a behaviour?
exercises.explanation: 'When did you stop X?' presupone que la persona estaba haciendo X y lo dejó de hacer.

exercises.question: A narrator who knows the thoughts of all characters and all events is called an _____ narrator.
exercises.explanation: El narrador omnisciente lo sabe todo sobre todos los personajes y la trama.

exercises.question: When a narrator's account contradicts evidence elsewhere in the text, they are called an _____ narrator.
exercises.explanation: El narrador no confiable da una versión de los hechos que no puede tomarse al pie de la letra.

exercises.question: When objects, characters, or events represent abstract ideas beyond their literal meaning throughout a whole text, this is called _____.
exercises.explanation: La alegoría es una representación sostenida de ideas abstractas a través de elementos narrativos concretos.

exercises.question: A recurring element — image, symbol, phrase, or idea — that reinforces central themes throughout a text is called a _____.
exercises.explanation: Un motivo literario es un elemento recurrente que refuerza o desarrolla los temas centrales de la obra.

exercises.question: When the audience knows something crucial that a character does not — such as knowing their trusted ally is actually an enemy — this is called _____.
exercises.explanation: La ironía dramática ocurre cuando el lector/espectador sabe algo que el personaje desconoce.

exercises.question: 'She was ruined. How could she have trusted him?' — third-person narration blending with a character's inner voice is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El discurso indirecto libre mezcla la perspectiva del narrador con los pensamientos del personaje sin señalización formal.

exercises.question: A writer's consistent and distinctive use of sentence length, diction, imagery, and tone constitutes their _____.
exercises.explanation: El estilo en prosa es el conjunto de elecciones lingüísticas que distinguen la escritura de un autor.

exercises.question: Subtle hints early in a narrative about events that will happen later is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El presagio narrativo (foreshadowing) prepara al lector para eventos futuros sin revelarlos explícitamente.

exercises.question: When a novel deliberately echoes, responds to, or transforms an earlier literary work, this relationship between texts is called _____.
exercises.explanation: La intertextualidad reconoce que los textos siempre dialogan con textos anteriores.

exercises.question: Aristotle argued that tragedy achieves _____ — an emotional purging through pity and fear — in the audience.
exercises.explanation: La catarsis aristotélica es la purga emocional que experimenta el espectador al presenciar una tragedia.

exercises.question: A poet's deliberate choice to use Latinate, polysyllabic words to create grandeur reflects conscious attention to _____.
exercises.explanation: La dicción es la elección deliberada de palabras; las palabras de origen latino tienden a sonar más formales y elevadas.

exercises.question: 'A stone lodged behind her ribs, pressing outward with every breath' makes grief concretely felt through _____.
exercises.explanation: La imaginería usa lenguaje sensorial y figurado para hacer concretas las experiencias abstractas.

exercises.question: When characters appear to discuss the weather but the real subject is unexpressed tension or desire, the unspoken layer of meaning is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El subtexto es el significado implícito detrás del diálogo que no se expresa directamente.

exercises.question: In Hamlet, Laertes serves as a _____ — a character whose contrasting traits highlight Hamlet's philosophical paralysis.
exercises.explanation: Un foil es un personaje cuyas características contrastantes resaltan las del protagonista.

exercises.question: The final section of a narrative in which loose ends are resolved and the conflict's outcome becomes clear is called the _____.
exercises.explanation: El desenlace es la fase final de la estructura narrativa donde se resuelven las tensiones del relato.

exercises.question: The use of an unreliable narrator always means the story is told in the first person.
exercises.answer: The use of an unreliable narrator does not necessarily mean the story is told in the first person — unreliability is defined by the questionability of the account, not by grammatical point of view.
exercises.explanation: Un narrador no confiable puede ser también de tercera persona; lo que lo define es que su versión es cuestionable.

exercises.question: Animal Farm is a metaphor for the Russian Revolution because each animal represents a historical figure.
exercises.answer: Animal Farm is an allegory for the Russian Revolution because each animal represents a historical figure.
exercises.explanation: Una alegoría es sostenida y sistemática; una metáfora es una comparación individual, no un sistema narrativo completo.

exercises.question: When the author writes 'the city was a prison without bars', this is a simile.
exercises.answer: When the author writes 'the city was a prison without bars', this is a metaphor.
exercises.explanation: Una metáfora afirma que algo ES otra cosa. Un símil usa 'like' o 'as': 'the city was like a prison'.

exercises.question: Dramatic irony occurs when a character says the opposite of what they mean.
exercises.answer: Verbal irony occurs when a character says the opposite of what they mean; dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something the character does not.
exercises.explanation: La ironía verbal = decir lo contrario de lo que se piensa; la ironía dramática = el lector sabe algo que el personaje ignora.

exercises.question: Stream of consciousness presents external events without comment or interpretation.
exercises.answer: Stream of consciousness presents the unfiltered flow of a character's thoughts and feelings as they occur in the mind.
exercises.explanation: El flujo de conciencia captura el pensamiento interior, no la narración objetiva de eventos externos.

exercises.question: The author's attitude toward their subject and audience, conveyed through word choice and style, is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El tono refleja la actitud del autor; el estado de ánimo (mood) es la atmósfera que experimenta el lector.

exercises.question: A moment of sudden insight or revelation — often about oneself or one's world — is called an _____.
exercises.explanation: La epifanía es el momento de iluminación súbita de un personaje, popularizado por James Joyce.

exercises.question: When someone says 'Oh, brilliant!' after something goes terribly wrong, meaning the opposite, this is an example of _____.
exercises.explanation: El sarcasmo es una forma de ironía verbal con intención burlona o hiriente.

exercises.question: A fire station that burns down is an example of _____ irony — when the outcome is the opposite of what would be expected.
exercises.explanation: La ironía situacional ocurre cuando la realidad contradice las expectativas de forma irónica.

exercises.question: Describing a devastating hurricane as 'a bit of bad weather' is extreme _____, often used for comic or ironic effect.
exercises.explanation: La subestimación expresa deliberadamente algo de manera menos intensa de lo que corresponde.

exercises.question: Delivering absurd or funny content without smiling or showing any emotion is a comedic style called _____.
exercises.explanation: El humor deadpan consiste en presentar lo cómico con total seriedad y sin señales emocionales visibles.

exercises.question: 'She had survived war, famine, exile — and now she couldn't find her keys.' The sudden drop from serious to trivial is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El bathos es el descenso abrupto de lo sublime a lo trivial, creando un efecto cómico.

exercises.question: Joking about your own failings or embarrassing moments to make an audience laugh is called _____.
exercises.explanation: El humor autodespreciativo usa los propios defectos del hablante como material cómico.

exercises.question: A novel that ridicules political corruption by depicting politicians as barnyard animals betraying their principles is an example of _____.
exercises.explanation: La sátira critica vicios humanos — especialmente en política — a través del ridículo y la exageración.

exercises.question: A text that imitates the style of a well-known work in an exaggerated way for comic effect is called a _____.
exercises.explanation: La parodia imita el estilo de un original de forma exagerada para producir humor.

exercises.question: When a reader knows a character is walking into a trap — information the character lacks — the text is using _____ irony.
exercises.explanation: La ironía dramática requiere que el lector/espectador sepa algo que el personaje ignora.

exercises.question: A pun exploits multiple _____ of a word — either multiple definitions or similar sounds — for humorous effect.
exercises.explanation: Un juego de palabras (pun) juega con la homofonía o la polisemia para producir humor.

exercises.question: Jokes that find comedy in death, suffering, or war are categorised as _____ humour.
exercises.explanation: El humor negro trata temas tabú de forma cómica, a menudo como mecanismo de defensa psicológica.

exercises.question: Most humour theorists agree that laughter arises from _____ — the gap between what we expect and what actually occurs.
exercises.explanation: La teoría de la incongruencia sostiene que el humor surge cuando se viola una expectativa de forma inesperada.

exercises.question: Oscar Wilde's wit is often described as _____ — sharp, biting, and occasionally cruel, but always elegant.
exercises.explanation: 'Acerbic' (acerbo/mordaz) describe un humor sharply critical y con frecuencia cortante.

exercises.question: When someone makes a comment that seems earnest on the surface but is clearly not meant to be taken seriously, we say it is _____.
exercises.explanation: 'Tongue-in-cheek' indica que una afirmación no debe tomarse literalmente; hay ironía detrás.

exercises.question: Soldiers and doctors often develop _____ humour — joking about death or disaster as a coping mechanism.
exercises.explanation: El humor de horca (gallows humour) encuentra comedia en situaciones terribles como mecanismo de afrontamiento.

exercises.question: Sarcasm and irony are the same: both involve saying what you mean in a subtle way.
exercises.answer: Sarcasm and irony are related but different: irony involves saying the opposite of what you mean, while sarcasm is a form of irony specifically used with intent to mock or wound.
exercises.explanation: La ironía es el principio general; el sarcasmo es una forma de ironía con intención crítica o hiriente.

exercises.question: A Modest Proposal by Swift, which ironically suggests eating Irish babies to solve poverty, is a parody.
exercises.answer: A Modest Proposal by Swift, which ironically suggests eating Irish babies to solve poverty, is a satire.
exercises.explanation: La sátira critica la sociedad o el poder; la parodia imita el estilo de una obra específica.

exercises.question: In a comedy of errors, when two characters unknowingly repeat the same joke to each other, this is dramatic irony.
exercises.answer: In a comedy of errors, when two characters unknowingly repeat the same joke to each other, this is situational irony.
exercises.explanation: La ironía situacional surge de las circunstancias; la ironía dramática requiere que el lector tenga información que el personaje no tiene.

exercises.question: Deadpan humour is effective because the comedian uses exaggerated facial expressions to signal the joke.
exercises.answer: Deadpan humour is effective because the comedian delivers the joke with a completely expressionless face, contrasting with the absurd content.
exercises.explanation: El deadpan funciona porque el comediante no muestra emoción alguna, contrastando con el contenido absurdo.

exercises.question: Bathos occurs when a narrative builds steadily toward a grand climax.
exercises.answer: Bathos occurs when a narrative suddenly drops from something grand or serious to something trivial, creating an anticlimax.
exercises.explanation: El bathos es lo opuesto al clímax: un descenso abrupto de lo elevado a lo ridículo.

exercises.question: A narrative tone that treats serious subjects with wry, emotionally detached amusement is called _____ detachment.
exercises.explanation: El distanciamiento irónico es una postura narrativa que mezcla agudeza y frialdad emocional.

exercises.question: The pause before a punchline — which creates anticipation and maximises comedic impact — is an aspect of _____.
exercises.explanation: El timing cómico es el control del ritmo y las pausas para maximizar el efecto humorístico.

exercises.question: Which rewrite of 'We decided to investigate the problem' best exemplifies formal academic style?
options: A decision was made to investigate the problem.
The decision to investigate was ours.
exercises.answer: A decision was made to investigate the problem.
exercises.explanation: La nominalización y la voz pasiva combinadas ocultan el agente y crean un tono formal e impersonal.

exercises.question: Which sentence is most appropriate for an academic paper reporting uncertain results?
options: This proves that X causes Y.
This suggests there may be a relationship between X and Y.
X definitely causes Y in all cases.
exercises.answer: This suggests there may be a relationship between X and Y.
exercises.explanation: El lenguaje de atenuación (hedging) evita afirmaciones absolutas cuando la evidencia es incompleta.

exercises.question: In legal and official writing, the passive voice is preferred because it _____ the agent of the action.
exercises.explanation: La voz pasiva elimina o relega al agente, produciendo un tono impersonal y formal.

exercises.question: 'Leverage synergies to drive stakeholder value' in a corporate context is an example of _____.
exercises.explanation: La jerga corporativa usa términos que suenan técnicos pero comunican poco contenido preciso.

exercises.question: Which represents an appropriate register shift from formal academic to plain language?
options: 'The outcomes are suboptimal' → 'The results were bad'
'The results were bad' → 'The outcomes are suboptimal'
'The findings are good' → 'Good findings were identified'
exercises.answer: 'The outcomes are suboptimal' → 'The results were bad'
exercises.explanation: El cambio hacia el lenguaje llano simplifica el vocabulario sin perder el significado.

exercises.question: Which sentence is an example of circumlocution that should be simplified?
options: Due to the fact that the experiment was unable to produce results of a positive nature, it cannot be deemed a success.
The experiment did not produce positive results.
exercises.answer: Due to the fact that the experiment was unable to produce results of a positive nature, it cannot be deemed a success.
exercises.explanation: El circunloquio usa muchas palabras donde pocas bastarían: 'The experiment failed'.

exercises.question: Which word does NOT typically function as a hedging device in academic writing?
exercises.explanation: 'Undeniably' es un intensificador, no un atenuador. Los atenuadores expresan incertidumbre.
